item.content:encoded:
Applications are open for the Fall 2027 graduate intake at Global Studies University in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates. Prospective students can apply for the two-year Master of Arts in Global African Studies or the five-year Doctor of Philosophy in Global Studies. The university also offers shorter certificate courses in Arabic, Amharic, Hausa and Kiswahili, with a separate Fall 2026 registration schedule.

Global Studies University, commonly abbreviated as GSU, presents an unusual academic proposition: postgraduate education designed around Africa, its global connections and the movement of ideas, people, cultures and institutions across regions. Rather than treating history, politics, culture, diplomacy, literature, heritage and language as isolated fields, GSU brings them together through interdisciplinary teaching and research.

The Fall 2027 degree application deadline is Tuesday, October 27, 2026. Applications opened on Monday, August 3, 2026. The first 40 applicants who submit complete applications for either graduate program are eligible for an application-fee waiver worth AED 365, according to the respective program pages. Applicants should therefore prepare and submit all required documents as early as possible.

For learners interested in a shorter language course, registration for the Fall 2026 Arabic, Amharic, Hausa and Kiswahili certificates has been extended to September 13, 2026, subject to available places. Classes run from September 14 to December 17, 2026.

This guide explains the programs, specializations, curriculum, admission requirements, English-language standards, tuition fees, scholarship support, application process, campus experience and important deadlines. Applicants should confirm the latest details through the official Global Studies University academic programs page before submitting an application.

Important GSU Application Dates

Program or activity Opening date Deadline or study period
Fall 2027 MA in Global African Studies applications August 3, 2026 October 27, 2026
Fall 2027 PhD in Global Studies applications August 3, 2026 October 27, 2026
Fall 2026 language-certificate registration Currently open Extended deadline: September 13, 2026
Fall 2026 language classes Not applicable September 14–December 17, 2026

GSU states in its frequently asked questions that admission decisions are generally released within 60 days after the relevant application deadline. A request to defer an admission offer should normally be submitted within seven days of receiving the offer, although deferral approval is not guaranteed.

About Global Studies University in Sharjah

Global Studies University is based in Al Manakh, Sharjah, United Arab Emirates. Its academic model combines the humanities, social sciences, arts and language study, with particular attention to Africa and its historical and contemporary relationships with other parts of the world.

The university operates from the restored former Khalid bin Mohammed School, a mid-1970s landmark. Its campus covers more than 23,000 square metres and includes:

  • Classrooms and collaborative learning spaces
  • A university library
  • Research archives
  • Galleries and exhibition areas
  • Student lounges
  • Courtyards
  • A café and bookshop
  • Recreational courts
  • Prayer rooms
  • Accessible washrooms and facilities
  • Parking areas

Africa Hall, first inaugurated in 1976 and reopened following renovation in 2018, provides a venue for conferences, public lectures, film programs and musical events. Additional information is available on the official GSU campus page.

GSU states that it is licensed by the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research through the Commission for Academic Accreditation. The university’s institutional licensure, MA program and PhD program are listed as active from January 2025 to January 2028. The institution reports that its two graduate degrees received accreditation on January 28, 2025. Prospective students can examine the university’s official accreditation information and should independently confirm whether the degrees satisfy any professional or academic recognition requirements relevant to their plans.

Programs Available at Global Studies University

GSU highlights three principal study routes:

  1. A two-year MA in Global African Studies.
  2. A five-year PhD in Global Studies.
  3. Short certificate courses in Arabic, Amharic, Hausa and Kiswahili for non-native speakers.

The MA and PhD are full-time, on-campus degrees taught in English in Sharjah. They are not advertised as online or distance-learning programs. The shorter language certificates follow a different structure and are available through online and hybrid delivery.

MA in Global African Studies

The MA in Global African Studies is a two-year, full-time, on-campus degree taught in English. It requires 36 credits and is intended for students seeking advanced interdisciplinary knowledge of Africa’s intellectual, political, social, cultural and international dimensions.

The curriculum combines common theory and methods courses, specialization courses, electives, African-language study, an internship and an independently researched thesis. Students select one of three tracks.

Museum and Critical Heritage Studies

The Museum and Critical Heritage Studies track investigates how museums, archives, archaeology, cultural property and heritage institutions influence interpretations of the past.

It examines questions involving ownership, restitution, colonial legacies, exhibition ethics, cultural representation and professional museum practice.

Published specialization courses include:

  • Who Owns the Past? Politics and Heritage in Africa
  • History and Theory of Museums
  • Decolonizing Heritage
  • Museum Collections Management and Politics of Exhibitions
  • Ethics, Archaeology and Heritage
  • Museum Management and Heritage as a Career

This track may appeal to applicants interested in museums, galleries, archives, cultural policy, archaeology, curatorial practice, collections management, heritage conservation or debates about the ownership and representation of cultural objects.

Diplomacy and Africa’s International Relations

This track concentrates on diplomacy, international relations, foreign policy, global governance, political economy and Africa’s historical and contemporary position within international society.

Published specialization courses include:

  • Diplomacy Studies
  • Advanced International Relations Theory
  • Africa in the World: Past and Present
  • Political Economy of Africa
  • International Finance and Global Economic Governance
  • State, International Society and Empire

The track may be relevant to students considering careers or further research in diplomacy, foreign affairs, government, international organizations, development, policy analysis, political economy and global governance.

Afro-Arab Relations

The Afro-Arab Relations track explores the long and complex interactions between African and Arab societies. Its historical scope extends from ancient periods through the Ottoman era and into modern political, intellectual and social formations.

Published courses include:

  • Introduction to Afro-Arab Relations: From Ancient Times to the Ottoman Empire
  • Comparative Slavery: The Transatlantic and Indian Ocean Worlds
  • Comparative Apartheid and Settler Colonialism: Palestine and South Africa
  • The Casablanca Group and Monrovia Group: The Formation of the Organisation of African Unity
  • Africa in the World: Past and Present
  • State, International Society and Empire

This track provides a structured foundation for studying the Red Sea, Indian Ocean networks, colonialism, slavery, liberation movements, international institutions and the political histories connecting African and Arab societies.

MA Program Structure

The 36-credit MA is organized as follows:

  • Six credits of common core courses
  • Eighteen credits of specialization core courses
  • Six credits of electives
  • A pass-or-fail language component
  • A pass-or-fail internship
  • A six-credit master’s thesis

The two common core courses are Theory and Method I and Theory and Method II.

Electives listed by GSU include:

  • Foreign Policy Analysis
  • Social and Political Thought in Africa
  • Government and Politics of Africa
  • The State in Africa

Every MA student studies one African language for three semesters. The available languages are Arabic, Amharic, Hausa and Kiswahili. Students receive a language certificate in addition to completing their degree requirements.

Students must also complete a thesis, which is written, examined and defended through a viva voce examination.

The required internship adds practical experience to the academic program. GSU’s career services advertise internship assistance, career advising, employability workshops, employer engagement, institutional visits and career events.

MA Admission Requirements

Prospective MA students should prepare the following:

  • A bachelor’s degree from an independently accredited institution recognized by the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research and GSU.
  • A minimum bachelor’s cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale or its equivalent.
  • An official bachelor’s transcript and graduation certificate with the required attestations.
  • A legal English translation of academic documents not originally issued in English.
  • A UAE Certificate of Recognition for a qualification awarded outside the UAE.
  • A valid passport.
  • A recent passport-sized photograph.
  • Emirates ID and UAE visa copies, where applicable.
  • IELTS Academic 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 91.
  • A current curriculum vitae.
  • Two recommendation letters issued within one month before application submission.
  • A Statement of Interest of approximately 1,000–1,500 words.
  • One substantial academic writing sample comparable to a journal article.
  • A national-service no-objection certificate where required for male Emirati applicants.
  • The AED 365 non-refundable application fee, unless the early complete-application waiver applies.

The Statement of Interest should explain the applicant’s personal and academic journey, motivation, future aspirations, suitability for GSU, research interests, proposed area of study and preferred MA track.

The academic writing sample can be an article, essay, book chapter, thesis chapter or comparable piece of scholarly work. A strong sample should demonstrate research ability, critical thinking, logical organization, evidence-based argument and appropriate academic referencing.

Shortlisted candidates may be invited to an interview in person or through Zoom. GSU states that applications remaining incomplete after the deadline will be rejected. The university also says that applicants previously dismissed from another institution for academic-integrity violations are not eligible for admission.

PhD in Global Studies

The PhD in Global Studies is a five-year, full-time, on-campus doctoral program taught in English. Its structure combines two years of coursework with approximately three years devoted to advanced research and the doctoral dissertation.

The program requires 81 credits:

  • Twenty-four credits of core coursework
  • Nine credits of language study
  • Twenty-four credits of electives
  • Six credits for reading and preparation for the A Examination
  • Eighteen credits for the doctoral project

The completed dissertation is evaluated and defended in a viva voce examination.

PhD Tracks and Concentrations

Applicants select one of two broad tracks.

Cultural, Visual and Literary Studies

This track includes three concentrations:

  • African Languages and Translation
  • History of Art, Visual and Performance Studies
  • Literary and Cultural Studies

It supports research involving language, translation, literature, cultural production, performance, visual culture, art history and connected forms of intellectual and creative expression.

Historical, Political and Social Studies

This track includes:

  • Historical Studies
  • Social and Political Studies

It supports doctoral work in history, politics, society, institutions, political economy, international relations and related interdisciplinary fields.

Across the tracks, GSU identifies seven thematic areas that can shape research and supervision:

  1. African-Arab Relations
  2. Intellectual Thought in Global Studies
  3. Diaspora
  4. Gender Studies and Feminist Futures
  5. Political Economy
  6. The Indian Ocean World
  7. The Muslim World

PhD Coursework and Language Study

The doctoral core covers subjects such as:

  • Globalization and Capitalism
  • Colonization and Decolonization
  • From Area Studies to Global Studies
  • Theory and Method
  • Summer Research Lab
  • African and African Diaspora Intellectual Tradition and Critical Imagination

Students complete six electives worth 24 credits in consultation with an adviser and the Director of Graduate Studies. Depending on the proposed dissertation, up to two electives may be taken outside the student’s primary track when they provide necessary research preparation.

Doctoral students also complete three semesters of a non-Western language, selecting Arabic, Amharic, Hausa or Kiswahili. This nine-credit requirement is intended to support direct engagement with sources, communities and scholarship relevant to each student’s research.

PhD Admission Requirements

GSU’s published doctoral requirements ask applicants to provide:

  • A bachelor’s or master’s qualification in a relevant humanities, social sciences or arts field from an independently accredited institution.
  • A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale or its equivalent.
  • A qualification from an institution recognized by the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research and GSU.
  • A bachelor’s program representing at least three years of study for equivalency purposes.
  • Official and attested bachelor’s and master’s transcripts and certificates, as applicable.
  • A UAE Certificate of Recognition for qualifications awarded outside the UAE.
  • Legal English translations of documents issued in another language.
  • A valid passport.
  • A recent passport photograph.
  • Emirates ID and UAE visa copies, where applicable.
  • IELTS Academic 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 91.
  • An up-to-date curriculum vitae.
  • A Statement of Interest of approximately 1,000–2,000 words.
  • A separate research statement of approximately 2,000–2,500 words.
  • Two substantial academic writing samples comparable to journal articles.
  • Two recommendation letters issued no more than one month before submission.
  • A national-service no-objection certificate where required for male Emirati applicants.
  • The AED 365 non-refundable application fee, unless an application-fee waiver applies.

The Statement of Interest should explain the applicant’s intellectual development, motivation, academic and professional aspirations, teaching or research experience, publications and other relevant preparation.

The separate research statement should present a coherent proposed project, identify the intended track, define the applicant’s specific research interests, explain previous preparation and describe the project’s anticipated academic, social or professional contribution.

Shortlisted PhD applicants are interviewed online through Zoom. Because doctoral admission depends strongly on academic and supervisory fit, applicants should explicitly connect their proposed projects with GSU’s tracks, concentrations and interdisciplinary themes.

English-Language Requirements

The standard English-language threshold for both graduate degrees is:

  • IELTS Academic: overall score of 6.5; or
  • TOEFL iBT: score of 91.

GSU’s frequently asked questions indicate that home-based or online IELTS examinations are not accepted. Applicants should take an accepted paper-based or computer-delivered academic examination and ensure that the score remains valid.

An English-language waiver may be considered, subject to institutional review, for a native English speaker with an English-medium degree or a graduate of an English-medium program who can document that an accepted IELTS or TOEFL threshold was required when entering that program.

Applicants should not assume that studying previously in English automatically guarantees a waiver. Anyone seeking an exemption should provide supporting evidence and obtain written confirmation from GSU.

Comprehensive GSU Graduate Scholarships

GSU advertises competitive scholarship assistance for admitted graduate students. The published support can include:

  • Full tuition coverage
  • UAE student-visa sponsorship
  • Health insurance
  • Air tickets for international students
  • Accommodation support
  • A monthly stipend
  • Research funding

The general funding pages do not publish the monthly stipend amount, research-funding limit or precise air-travel entitlement. Applicants should request the current financial terms before making travel, housing or enrollment commitments.

Most importantly, admission and scholarship selection are separate processes. An applicant who receives admission to the MA or PhD is not automatically guaranteed financial support.

GSU’s funding pages refer to a 3.5 out of 4.0 academic threshold in the relevant previous degree or degrees. However, different sections of the published scholarship information use slightly different language about whether the threshold must apply to one or multiple previous qualifications. Applicants should confirm how the requirement applies to their academic history directly with Admissions or Academic Affairs.

Scholarship recipients must normally:

  • Enroll full time, ordinarily for six to 12 credits per semester.
  • Maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0.
  • Remain in good academic standing.
  • Avoid unnecessary course withdrawals or conduct that delays academic progress.
  • Comply with academic-integrity and student-conduct requirements.
  • Obtain permission or provide notification before travelling outside the UAE.
  • Remain in the approved academic program.
  • Avoid holding another scholarship simultaneously unless GSU approves an equivalent alternative arrangement.

Academic underperformance, academic-integrity violations, misconduct or failure to comply with scholarship conditions can lead to termination of financial support.

Prospective applicants should examine the official MA scholarships and financial-aid page or PhD financial-support page for current terms.

Tuition Fees and Additional Charges

Students who do not receive full financial support should plan carefully for tuition and related costs.

Published MA Tuition

GSU lists the MA tuition rate as AED 7,288 per credit. At 36 credits, the published base calculation is:

  • Thirty program credits: AED 218,640
  • Six dissertation credits: AED 43,728
  • Base total: AED 262,368

Published PhD Tuition

GSU lists the PhD tuition rate as AED 7,891 per credit. At 81 credits, the published base calculation is:

  • Sixty-three program credits: AED 497,133
  • Eighteen doctoral-project credits: AED 142,038
  • Base total: AED 639,171

These totals are mathematical calculations based on the published credit rates and do not necessarily represent every amount payable. Additional charges and 5 percent VAT may apply.

Other published charges include:

  • AED 365 non-refundable application fee
  • AED 3,000 non-refundable registration deposit
  • AED 200 thesis or extension-related fee
  • AED 500 first-time residence reservation fee, which is described as non-refundable but deductible from residence fees
  • AED 200 utility-service fee
  • AED 500 late-payment, returned-cheque or declined-card charge in applicable cases

The published refund schedule generally provides:

  1. A 100 percent tuition refund before the end of the first week, excluding non-refundable deposits.
  2. A 50 percent tuition refund during the second week.
  3. A 25 percent tuition refund during the third week.
  4. No tuition refund after the third week.

A tuition deposit may be refunded when a student visa is refused and satisfactory evidence is submitted. This provision does not apply in the same manner to fully funded students. Applicants should examine the official MA tuition information or PhD tuition information before paying.

GSU also advertises a 30 percent first-semester tuition discount. Different sections of the university’s published information appear to use different GPA thresholds for this discount. Applicants should obtain written confirmation of the current academic threshold, whether the discount is automatic or competitive, and whether any other limitations apply.

The discount cannot ordinarily be combined with a scholarship or another tuition waiver and normally requires the recipient to maintain a GPA of at least 3.0.

Fall 2026 Arabic, Amharic, Hausa and Kiswahili Courses

GSU’s language certificate program is designed for non-native speakers seeking structured instruction in Arabic, Amharic, Hausa or Kiswahili.

For Fall 2026, the university lists Elementary I and Intermediate I levels. Program features include:

  • Twelve weeks of instruction
  • Twenty-four sessions
  • Thirty-six contact hours
  • Two 90-minute sessions per week
  • Online and hybrid delivery options
  • A published course fee of AED 1,440
  • Discounts of up to 15 percent in eligible cases
  • A free placement test for applicants seeking entry above Elementary Level I
  • A completion certificate issued by GSU under licensing from the Sharjah Private Education Authority

The teaching model develops speaking, listening, reading and writing while introducing relevant cultural knowledge.

The Fall 2026 courses run from September 14 to December 17, 2026. The extended registration deadline is September 13, 2026, and places are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

Foreign Degree Recognition and Attestation

Applicants educated outside the UAE should begin the recognition process early. GSU requires overseas qualifications to receive a Certificate of Recognition from the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research.

Depending on the country and document, applicants may need authentication by:

  1. The institution that issued the qualification.
  2. The responsible education authority in the country of study.
  3. The foreign affairs ministry in that country.
  4. The appropriate UAE embassy or consulate.
  5. Relevant UAE authorities after arrival, where required.

Applicants should follow the official UAE recognition process and GSU’s instructions rather than relying only on an informal translation or scanned copy. Original records may be requested for verification following arrival.

How to Apply to Global Studies University

Step 1: Select the Appropriate Program and Track

Review the structure, research areas and career relevance of the MA and PhD. MA applicants must select one of the three specializations. PhD applicants should identify the broad track, concentration and themes that best match their intended research.

Step 2: Confirm Recognition of Previous Qualifications

Verify that the awarding institution is independently accredited and recognized by the UAE Ministry and GSU. International applicants should begin the UAE Certificate of Recognition process as early as possible.

Step 3: Arrange an Accepted English Test

Book an accepted IELTS Academic or TOEFL iBT examination if a valid result is not already available. Do not assume that an online or home-based examination will be accepted.

Step 4: Request Recent Recommendation Letters

Both degree programs require two recommendation letters issued within one month before the application is submitted. Applicants should brief their referees in advance while coordinating the issue date carefully.

Step 5: Prepare the Written Application Materials

Complete the applicable Statement of Interest, research statement and academic writing samples. Every document should be specific, organized and aligned with the selected program.

PhD applicants should present an original but manageable research problem, suitable methods and a credible explanation of the sources or evidence they intend to use.

Step 6: Collect Academic and Identity Documents

Gather the passport, photograph, transcripts, certificates, translations, attestations, recognition records, Emirates ID and visa copies where applicable, and the national-service document where required.

Step 7: Submit a Complete Online Application

Begin through the official GSU application portal. Upload every required document, pay the application fee unless a waiver applies, and save the submission confirmation.

Step 8: Prepare for the Selection Interview

Shortlisted candidates should be ready to discuss their academic background, reasons for choosing GSU, intended track, proposed research and how the degree connects with their longer-term goals.

Step 9: Review Admission and Scholarship Decisions Separately

An admission offer does not confirm a scholarship. Applicants should read every decision letter carefully and obtain clarification about funding, visa sponsorship, accommodation and enrollment deposits before accepting.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application

  • Apply early because the fee waiver is limited to the first 40 complete applications for each graduate program.
  • Follow every published word limit.
  • Refer specifically to the selected track and relevant GSU research themes.
  • Submit a writing sample that demonstrates a focused research question, logical organization, evidence-based analysis and academic integrity.
  • Ensure the proposed research is realistic and sufficiently focused.
  • Coordinate recommendation-letter dates carefully because letters must be recently issued.
  • Request written clarification about scholarship or tuition-discount conditions when the published wording is unclear.
  • Budget on the assumption that expenses remain the student’s responsibility until a scholarship is formally confirmed.
  • Keep copies of submitted documents, correspondence, test results and payment receipts.
  • Do not wait until the deadline to begin UAE degree-recognition and attestation procedures.

Student Visa, Accommodation and Family Considerations

International students normally require a UAE student visa. GSU states that it sponsors admitted international students and provides detailed instructions following admission. Final visa approval remains subject to UAE immigration rules.

The university does not currently provide on-campus student housing. It assists students with off-campus arrangements and identifies The Nest at Aljada, approximately 12 kilometres from campus, as a recommended residence.

The accommodation advertises:

  • Shared and private room arrangements
  • Separate provisions for male and female residents
  • Furnished rooms
  • Utilities and Wi-Fi
  • Security
  • Study and library spaces
  • Recreation and gaming spaces
  • Sports facilities
  • Pools and gyms

Applicants should confirm current availability, transportation and costs before making a commitment. Scholarship-supported accommodation should not automatically be interpreted as an on-campus room. More information is available through the GSU student residences page.

GSU indicates that family members may accompany a student where immigration rules permit, but the university does not pay family expenses. Students planning to relocate with dependants should budget separately for visas, housing, health insurance, education and everyday living costs.

Employment and Career Development During Study

The graduate degrees require full-time commitment. According to GSU, scholarship students or research assistants may undertake limited work of up to eight hours per week under the applicable rules.

MA students may do so only during their second academic year, while PhD students may do so only during their third year. Students should receive formal approval and ensure that any employment complies with scholarship, visa and academic regulations.

GSU’s career services include:

  • Individual career advising
  • Internship assistance
  • Employability workshops
  • Employer engagement
  • Organizational visits
  • Career events and career days

These services can help students connect interdisciplinary research, language competence and regional expertise with careers in education, policy, government, diplomacy, museums, heritage, media, civil society, research and international organizations.

Career outcomes depend on each student’s background, academic performance, professional networks and applicable employment regulations. Admission to the university does not guarantee employment.

Questions to Ask Before Accepting an Offer

Applicants may wish to request written answers to these questions:

  1. Is the previous qualification fully recognized for GSU admission and UAE equivalency?
  2. Has the English-language requirement been satisfied or formally waived?
  3. Is the admission offer unconditional?
  4. Has a scholarship been awarded separately from admission?
  5. What exact stipend, travel, accommodation and research-funding amounts apply?
  6. Which GPA rule applies to the scholarship or first-semester discount?
  7. Which deposits, fees and taxes remain payable with financial support?
  8. What is the semester-by-semester payment schedule for self-funded students?
  9. Which faculty members and research resources align with the proposed project?
  10. Which visa and accommodation steps must be completed before arrival?

Degree-admission questions can be sent to admissions@gsu.ac.ae. Language-course questions can be sent to languages@gsu.ac.ae.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the Fall 2027 graduate application deadline?

The deadline for both the MA in Global African Studies and the PhD in Global Studies is Tuesday, October 27, 2026. Applications opened on August 3, 2026.

Are the GSU graduate programs available online?

No. The MA and PhD are advertised as full-time, on-campus programs in Sharjah. The separate language certificates have online and hybrid options.

Does every admitted graduate student receive a scholarship?

No. Scholarships are competitive. An admission offer does not automatically include funding.

What can the scholarship cover?

The advertised package can include full tuition, UAE visa sponsorship, health insurance, air tickets for international students, accommodation, a monthly stipend and research funds. Applicants should confirm the exact value and conditions through their award documents.

What GPA is required?

Graduate admission generally requires at least 3.0 out of 4.0 or the equivalent. The scholarship pages refer to a higher 3.5 threshold in the relevant previous degree or degrees. Applicants should confirm how the scholarship rule applies to their qualifications.

What English score is required?

The published standard is IELTS Academic 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 91. Any waiver is subject to review and supporting evidence.

Is there an application fee?

Yes. The standard non-refundable fee is AED 365. According to the program pages, the first 40 applicants who complete an application for either Fall 2027 graduate degree can receive an application-fee waiver.

Can international students apply?

Yes. GSU publishes procedures covering international applicants, overseas qualifications, student visas and international-student travel support. Every candidate must still satisfy the academic, documentation, English-language and immigration requirements.

When is the Fall 2026 language-course deadline?

The extended registration deadline is September 13, 2026. Classes run from September 14 to December 17, 2026, subject to available places.

Conclusion

Global Studies University’s Fall 2027 intake offers an interdisciplinary route into postgraduate study in Sharjah. The MA in Global African Studies integrates theory, specialization, African-language learning, an internship and a research thesis across museum and heritage studies, diplomacy and African international relations, or Afro-Arab relations.

The PhD in Global Studies offers an extended research pathway spanning cultural, literary, visual, historical, political and social inquiry. Its themes include diaspora, gender, political economy, the Indian Ocean, the Muslim world and African-Arab connections.

GSU’s competitive scholarship package is potentially extensive, but applicants must distinguish clearly between admission and funding. No applicant should make financial plans based on scholarship support until a formal award has been issued.

Degree recognition, document attestation, recent recommendation letters, English testing and substantial written submissions also make early preparation essential. Candidates for the Fall 2027 MA or PhD should submit complete applications well before October 27, 2026. Learners seeking the shorter Fall 2026 language certificates must act sooner because the extended registration deadline is September 13, 2026 and places are limited.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for Cohort 3 of the Yale Teaching Fellowship, an intensive graduate education and teacher-preparation initiative designed to build a strong, diverse and long-term teaching workforce for New Haven Public Schools in Connecticut, United States.

Developed through a partnership among Yale University, New Haven Public Schools, New Haven Promise and Southern Connecticut State University, the program combines fully funded graduate tuition with teacher certification, structured classroom experience, mentorship and a clear route into high-need teaching roles. Depending on the selected track, participants can earn either a Master of Arts in Teaching or a Master of Science from Southern Connecticut State University while preparing to serve New Haven students.

The fellowship concentrates primarily on mathematics, science and special education, which New Haven Public Schools has identified as major teacher-shortage areas. Yale’s current program information states that applications for Cohort 3 are open and must be completed by January 1, 2027.

Yale Teaching Fellowship Cohort 3 at a Glance

Program detail Information
Program name Yale Teaching Fellowship
Cohort Cohort 3
Lead funder Yale University
Academic institution Southern Connecticut State University
School district New Haven Public Schools
Recruitment and applicant support partner New Haven Promise
Location New Haven, Connecticut, United States
Main subject areas Mathematics, science and special education
Available routes Teacher Pipeline Track and Current Teachers Track
Graduate awards Master of Arts in Teaching or Master of Science, depending on track
Tuition support Full tuition for both tracks
Living support $47,380 during the first fellowship year for Teacher Pipeline Track fellows
Places per fellowship year Up to 20 Teacher Pipeline fellows and up to five Current Teacher fellows
Service requirement At least three years of full-time service after completing the relevant degree program
Application deadline January 1, 2027
Application status Open

What Is the Yale Teaching Fellowship?

The Yale Teaching Fellowship is a service-linked graduate training program created to address persistent teacher shortages and strengthen teacher retention in New Haven Public Schools. It is not a conventional Yale degree program: fellows complete their graduate degrees at Southern Connecticut State University, while Yale provides substantial financial support and helps sustain the wider fellowship structure.

The fellowship emerged from the Yale & Slavery Research Project and reflects Yale’s broader commitment to New Haven. It is designed to recruit high-quality educators from varied backgrounds and experiences, prepare them for difficult-to-fill teaching areas and support them beyond initial certification so they can build lasting careers in the district.

According to the current Yale Teaching Fellowship program page, the initiative represents a $10 million investment over six years. Across four fellowship years beginning in May 2025, it aims to place up to 100 master’s-qualified educators in New Haven’s public schools. That total is expected to include up to 80 new teachers and up to 20 current teachers gaining a special education cross-endorsement.

The program is already producing cohorts of classroom-ready educators. Yale reported in August 2026 that the first cohort of 20 fellows had completed its preparation year and that the second cohort included 18 participants: eight in special education, six in science and four in mathematics.

Why the Yale Teaching Fellowship Matters

The Yale Teaching Fellowship was built around a straightforward problem: public-school systems need well-prepared teachers, but financial barriers, the cost of graduate education and limited access to extended classroom training can prevent promising candidates from entering or remaining in the profession.

The fellowship addresses those barriers through an integrated model that includes:

  • Full graduate tuition rather than partial tuition assistance;
  • A substantial first-year living stipend for eligible Teacher Pipeline fellows;
  • A degree pathway aligned with Connecticut teacher certification;
  • Extended clinical experience in New Haven Public Schools;
  • Guidance from experienced mentor teachers;
  • A cohort-based learning experience;
  • A transition from graduate study to responsibility as a teacher of record; and
  • Ongoing mentorship during the required period of service.

This structure gives aspiring teachers time to develop their skills before assuming full classroom responsibility. It also enables current teachers to gain specialist qualifications in an area where the district has identified a serious need.

The Four Partner Institutions and Their Roles

Yale University

Yale supplies the program’s principal financial investment. It covers full tuition for fellows in both tracks and provides the advertised $47,380 first-year living stipend to Teacher Pipeline Track participants. Yale also supports the cohort experience and the fellowship’s broader mission of serving and strengthening New Haven.

Southern Connecticut State University

Southern Connecticut State University provides the graduate education. Teacher Pipeline fellows work toward a Master of Arts in Teaching and initial Connecticut teacher certification, while eligible current teachers pursue a Master of Science and special education cross-endorsement.

SCSU independently controls admission to its degree programs, so selection as a fellowship finalist does not by itself guarantee university admission.

New Haven Public Schools

New Haven Public Schools identifies the staffing areas that the program should prioritize. The district supplies classroom settings, mentor teachers, residency placements and the employment environment in which fellows complete their required service.

New Haven Promise

New Haven Promise assists with recruitment, application support and professional guidance. Its involvement helps connect the fellowship to New Haven residents, school employees and candidates who have demonstrated a commitment to the city and its young people.

Priority Teaching Areas

Southern Connecticut State University has developed fellowship-aligned academic schedules in three main areas identified by New Haven Public Schools:

  1. Mathematics;
  2. Science; and
  3. Special education.

Science pathways may include biology, chemistry, earth science or physics, subject to the candidate’s academic preparation and SCSU’s admission requirements.

The Teacher Pipeline Track may consider a candidate seeking another licensure area if that person can complete the selected program within the same timeframe as the priority programs. However, the fellowship gives preference to mathematics, science and special education because these represent the district’s greatest teacher shortages.

Teacher Pipeline Track

The Teacher Pipeline Track is the main entry route for college graduates who do not already hold a teaching certificate. New Haven Public Schools paraprofessionals and other student-facing support staff are especially encouraged to consider this pathway, although selected participants must comply with the track’s employment conditions during the first fellowship year.

Up to 20 college graduates may enter this track in each fellowship year. Participants pursue Connecticut teacher certification and a two-year Master of Arts in Teaching at Southern Connecticut State University. The advertised academic sequence covers five terms: fall, spring, summer, fall and spring.

Financial Support for Teacher Pipeline Fellows

Yale provides:

  • Full tuition for the relevant SCSU graduate program;
  • A living stipend of $47,380 during the first fellowship year, covering September through August; and
  • A structured cohort experience.

The published stipend applies specifically to the Teacher Pipeline Track. Applicants should not assume that the Current Teachers Track carries the same living allowance.

Training Sequence

The track deliberately increases classroom responsibility over time:

  • During the fall of the first year, fellows spend 20 hours per week in a fellowship mentor’s classroom.
  • During the spring of the first year, fellows undertake a full-time teacher residency in their school.
  • During the second year, fellows work as full-time teachers of record under Connecticut’s Resident Educator Certificate while continuing the degree pathway.
  • After completing the degree, fellows commit to at least three years of teaching in New Haven Public Schools and receive ongoing mentorship.

This sequence is designed to avoid placing new teachers into classrooms without sufficient preparation. Fellows first observe and assist, then complete a full-time residency, and finally move into paid professional responsibility as teachers of record.

Current Teachers Track

The Current Teachers Track is designed for eligible full-time teachers already working in New Haven Public Schools. Its purpose is to help qualified educators gain a Connecticut cross-endorsement in special education while earning an SCSU Master of Science.

Up to five certified teachers may enter this track per fellowship year. The graduate program runs across four semesters—summer, fall, spring and summer—and Yale pays full tuition.

Participants continue working as full-time NHPS teachers while completing the program. After earning the Master of Science and cross-endorsement, they must secure and serve in a full-time special education teaching position in the district for at least three years.

This track does not train participants for their first teaching credential. It develops currently certified district teachers for difficult-to-fill special education positions.

Major Benefits of the Yale Teaching Fellowship

Full Graduate Tuition

Both fellowship tracks provide full tuition support for the applicable SCSU master’s degree. This removes one of the largest financial barriers facing prospective and current educators seeking advanced qualifications.

$47,380 First-Year Living Stipend

Teacher Pipeline fellows receive a living stipend of $47,380 during their first year, from September through August. This support is particularly important because the training progresses from a 20-hour weekly placement to a full-time residency.

Master’s Degree and Professional Credential

Depending on the track, participants can earn an SCSU Master of Arts in Teaching with initial Connecticut certification or an SCSU Master of Science with special education cross-endorsement.

Sustained Classroom Experience

The fellowship combines academic learning with direct practice. Pipeline fellows receive mentor-classroom experience, a full-time residency and a supported transition into teaching as the responsible instructor.

Mentorship and Cohort Support

Fellows learn alongside a cohort and receive guidance from experienced educators. Ongoing mentorship continues during the post-degree service period for Teacher Pipeline fellows.

Route Into a High-Need Public-Service Career

The program prepares participants for roles in subjects where qualified teachers are urgently needed. The service commitment links the public investment directly to students and schools in New Haven.

Application Materials

Applicants should prepare a complete application carefully and allow sufficient time for transcripts and recommendations. The published track requirements identify the following materials:

  • Responses to short-answer questions;
  • Responses to essay questions;
  • A résumé or curriculum vitae;
  • Transcripts from every college or university attended; and
  • A letter of recommendation.

For Teacher Pipeline applicants, the recommendation should come from a professor, mentor or supervisor. For Current Teachers Track applicants, it should come from an NHPS principal or assistant principal.

Applicants with degrees earned outside the United States should be prepared to provide a certified course-by-course evaluation from World Education Services or Educational Credential Evaluators, as required by the fellowship and SCSU.

The online form allows applicants to save an incomplete application and receive a return link. Candidates should copy or email that link to themselves so they can continue working before final submission. An application should be treated as complete only when every required document, including the recommendation and transcripts, has been received.

Southern Connecticut State University Admission Process

Fellowship finalists must separately apply for admission to the appropriate Southern Connecticut State University graduate program. This is a mandatory second process. SCSU evaluates academic eligibility and retains sole discretion over admission decisions.

For Master of Arts in Teaching programs, the SCSU 2026–2027 graduate catalogue lists a bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution, or a recognized foreign equivalent, with a total undergraduate GPA of at least 2.70.

Depending on the subject, applicants may also need appropriate subject-area preparation, general-education coursework and Praxis Core or qualifying substitute scores.

The current catalogue explains that most MAT concentrations require content preparation in the proposed endorsement area. It also lists 39 general-education credits distributed across five of six subject areas, including a three-credit United States history survey course, for MAT programs other than comprehensive special education.

SCSU may consider applicants with limited outstanding coursework for conditional admission, but university and certification requirements must still be completed.

Applicants should review the exact SCSU concentration requirements that apply to mathematics, biology, chemistry, earth science, physics or comprehensive special education. Minimum eligibility does not guarantee either fellowship selection or university admission.

Academic and Service Obligations

The Yale Teaching Fellowship is a significant funded commitment rather than an unrestricted scholarship. Fellows are expected to:

  • Maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 at SCSU;
  • Complete the approved degree and certification or cross-endorsement pathway;
  • Participate fully in the required in-person academic and school-based activities; and
  • Complete at least three years of full-time qualifying teaching service after finishing the degree.

Published fellowship terms also state that a participant who does not complete the required three years of employment may have to repay part of the fellowship funding.

The previously published repayment schedule lists:

  • $10,000 for completing less than one year;
  • $6,666 for completing more than one but less than two years; and
  • $3,333 for completing more than two but less than three years.

Applicants must check the final Cohort 3 agreement before accepting an award because that agreement will control the binding financial and service conditions.

The published terms further explain that if a fellow is not offered a full-time NHPS teaching position by July 31 of the year in which the fellow earns the SCSU degree, the service commitment may be completed in another Connecticut Alliance District after advance notice.

This provision should not be treated as an automatic job guarantee. Applicants should verify its operation directly with the fellowship team.

Yale Teaching Fellowship Cohort 3 Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for Cohort 3 is:

January 1, 2027

Yale’s current program page confirms that applications are open. Because no submission time or late-application policy is stated on the public Yale page, candidates should submit well before the final day.

Transcripts, international credential evaluations and recommendation letters can take time to arrange, and all required materials should be received before the deadline.

How to Apply for the Yale Teaching Fellowship

Applicants can use the following process:

  1. Read the current fellowship overview and compare the two tracks.
  2. Select the track that matches your existing certification and employment status.
  3. Review the relevant SCSU degree and Connecticut certification requirements.
  4. Arrange transcripts from every college or university attended.
  5. Obtain a WES or ECE evaluation if presenting an international degree.
  6. Ask an appropriate recommender early and explain the deadline.
  7. Prepare the short-answer and essay responses with clear evidence of readiness to teach and serve New Haven students.
  8. Upload the résumé or CV and all supporting documents.
  9. Save the in-progress application link securely if the form is not completed in one session.
  10. Submit the complete fellowship application before January 1, 2027.
  11. If selected as a finalist, complete the separate application to Southern Connecticut State University.

Applicants should begin from the official Cohort 3 information page and cross-check updates on the Yale Office of New Haven Affairs program page.

Questions about the fellowship may be directed to Christine Gentry, Director of the Yale Teaching Fellowship, at christine.gentry@yale.edu.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

A competitive application should do more than state a general interest in education. It should demonstrate that the applicant understands the fellowship’s purpose and is ready for its academic, practical and service requirements.

Candidates should consider the following:

  • Explain why teaching in New Haven Public Schools is a serious long-term commitment rather than a temporary opportunity.
  • Connect academic background or professional experience to mathematics, science, special education or another demonstrable district need.
  • Use specific examples of work with children, families, schools or community organizations.
  • Describe experiences that helped create inclusive, supportive or equitable environments for school-aged children.
  • Show readiness for an intensive sequence combining graduate study and substantial in-person classroom work.
  • Address the three-year service obligation directly and realistically.
  • Proofread every written response and ensure that the résumé, essays and recommendation present a consistent professional story.
  • If applicable, explain how first-generation or low-income experience has shaped the applicant’s understanding of educational opportunity, without assuming that personal background alone is enough for selection.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the graduate degree awarded by Yale University?

No. Yale funds and supports the fellowship, but the graduate degree is awarded by Southern Connecticut State University.

Does every fellow receive the $47,380 living stipend?

No. The currently advertised living stipend applies to Teacher Pipeline Track fellows during the first fellowship year. The Current Teachers Track advertises full tuition but does not advertise the same stipend.

Can a person apply for a subject other than mathematics, science or special education?

Possibly, under the Teacher Pipeline Track, if the proposed licensure program can be completed within the same timeframe. However, the program gives preference to mathematics, science and special education because those are the principal shortage areas identified by NHPS.

Can current NHPS paraprofessionals or student-facing support employees apply?

Yes. They are specifically encouraged to consider the Teacher Pipeline Track. However, the published Pipeline eligibility conditions state that fellows cannot remain NHPS employees during the first fellowship year, so affected applicants should clarify the employment transition before accepting an offer.

Is the program fully online?

No. It requires in-person study at SCSU and direct work in New Haven Public Schools. Applicants must live, or be able to live by the start of the fellowship, close enough to participate fully.

Does the fellowship guarantee a permanent teaching job?

Applicants should not treat it as an unconditional employment guarantee. The program creates a strong preparation and service pathway, and published terms address what happens if NHPS does not offer a full-time position by a specified date, but candidates should verify employment conditions directly.

When is the deadline?

The Cohort 3 application deadline is January 1, 2027.

Conclusion

The Yale Teaching Fellowship Cohort 3 offers an unusually comprehensive route into high-need public-school teaching. By combining full graduate tuition, Connecticut certification pathways, extensive classroom preparation, mentorship and a substantial first-year stipend for eligible Pipeline fellows, the program reduces both the financial and professional barriers that often prevent talented candidates from becoming teachers.

The opportunity also carries serious responsibilities. Fellows must meet SCSU’s admission and academic standards, participate in an intensive in-person program and complete a multi-year teaching commitment. Prospective applicants should therefore assess their eligibility, location, work authorization, subject preparation and long-term commitment to New Haven before applying.

Applications are open, and all required materials should be submitted by January 1, 2027.

item.content:encoded:
The Yenching Academy of Peking University Scholarship 2027 offers an exceptional opportunity for outstanding students from China and around the world to pursue an interdisciplinary graduate education focused on China at Peking University in Beijing, China.

Through the Yenching Academy, approximately 120 new students are enrolled annually, bringing together students from the Chinese Mainland and international students to study, live and learn in a highly diverse academic environment. International students make up approximately 75% of the student body, creating an environment in which scholars from different countries and academic backgrounds can engage with one another and develop a deeper understanding of China.

The programme is designed for academically outstanding students who have a strong interest in the interdisciplinary study of China and who can demonstrate extracurricular achievements, community engagement, social responsibility and leadership potential.

One of the most attractive aspects of the Yenching Academy opportunity is its generous fellowship package. Selected Yenching Scholars receive support covering tuition fees, accommodation, a monthly stipend, one round-trip travel fare and field study costs.

For the 2027 cohort, applications from international candidates and candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions open on September 1, 2026, with the application deadline set for November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time.

About the Yenching Academy of Peking University

The Yenching Academy is a graduate-level academic programme at Peking University, one of China’s leading universities.

The Academy brings together students from China and other parts of the world with the aim of encouraging interdisciplinary learning and deeper engagement with China.

Rather than restricting students to a single narrow academic discipline, the programme emphasizes an interdisciplinary approach to the study of China. This allows scholars with different academic backgrounds and interests to explore China from multiple perspectives.

The Academy’s international composition is also an important part of the programme. Approximately 120 new students are admitted each year, with international students accounting for roughly 75 percent of the student body.

This creates opportunities for students to develop international networks while studying alongside peers from different countries, academic disciplines and cultural backgrounds.

What Is the Yenching Academy Scholarship?

The Yenching Academy provides a generous fellowship to all scholars admitted to the programme.

The fellowship is intended to provide comprehensive financial support for selected students during their studies.

The fellowship includes:

  • Tuition fees
  • Accommodation
  • Monthly stipend
  • One round-trip travel fare
  • Field study costs

This combination of financial benefits makes the Yenching Academy particularly attractive to students seeking an internationally oriented graduate education in China with substantial financial support.

Yenching Academy 2027 Application Timeline

Applications for the 2027 cohort from international candidates and candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions open on:

September 1, 2026

The application deadline is:

November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time

Applicants should pay close attention to the time zone because the deadline is specified according to Beijing time, rather than the applicant’s local time.

Students should also begin preparing their application materials well before the deadline because the application requires several documents, including academic records, recommendation letters, a personal statement, a research-interest statement and proof of English proficiency where applicable.

Who Can Apply for the Yenching Academy?

The Yenching Academy welcomes applications from both Chinese Mainland candidates and students from abroad, although the application procedures differ depending on the applicant’s location and status.

The Academy generally expects applicants to demonstrate strong academic performance, intellectual curiosity, interest in China and evidence of leadership and community engagement.

Applicants should meet the following core qualifications.

1. Bachelor’s Degree or Current Bachelor’s Student

Applicants must either:

  • Hold a minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in any field; or
  • Be currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s programme and expect to receive their diploma by August of the intended enrollment year.

This means that students who have not yet completed their undergraduate education may still be eligible if they are expected to graduate by the specified date.

The Academy does not restrict the Bachelor’s degree to a particular discipline. Applicants from different academic backgrounds can therefore be considered as long as they satisfy the other requirements.

2. Outstanding Academic Record

Applicants are expected to have an outstanding academic record.

Academic excellence is an important part of the Yenching Academy selection process because the programme is designed for high-achieving students capable of engaging with rigorous graduate-level interdisciplinary study.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their transcripts accurately demonstrate their academic strengths.

3. Strong Interest in the Interdisciplinary Study of China

A key requirement is a strong interest in interdisciplinary study of China.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate why they want to study China and how their academic, professional, research or personal interests connect with the interdisciplinary focus of the Academy.

A generic interest in studying abroad may not adequately demonstrate this requirement. Applicants should instead develop a clear explanation of the questions, issues or areas concerning China that they want to explore.

4. Extracurricular Achievement and Community Engagement

The Academy also looks for applicants with a record of:

  • Extracurricular achievement
  • Community engagement
  • Social responsibility
  • Leadership potential

This means that academic performance is not the only consideration.

Applicants should demonstrate how they have contributed beyond the classroom, whether through community initiatives, student organizations, volunteering, professional activities, social-impact projects, leadership roles or other meaningful engagements.

The strongest applications should show evidence of initiative and a willingness to contribute to communities beyond one’s immediate academic environment.

5. English Proficiency

Applicants must demonstrate sufficient English proficiency unless they fall within an exemption category specified by the Academy.

The required minimum scores include:

  • IELTS Academic: Overall 7.0
  • TOEFL iBT: Overall 100
  • Cambridge English Scale (Advanced): Overall 185
  • CET 6: Overall 600
  • TEM 4: Pass level of “良好” or above

Applicants should carefully determine which English-language qualification applies to them and ensure that their test results meet the minimum requirement.

English Language Test Exemptions

Not every applicant is required to submit an English proficiency test report.

International applicants whose native language is English do not need to provide an English proficiency test report.

Applicants who have graduated from an English-taught degree programme at undergraduate level or above are also exempt from providing an English proficiency test report.

However, there is an important exception for applicants from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions.

Applicants from these regions must provide an English proficiency test report even if they have attended or graduated from an English-taught degree programme.

Without an English proficiency test report, such candidates will need to take English as a Second Language after enrolling at Peking University.

For applicants from the Chinese Mainland, an English proficiency test report is a compulsory application material.

Validity Period for English Tests

The Yenching Academy specifies that English proficiency tests must have been taken after September 1, 2025.

Applicants should therefore check the date of their examination before submitting their application.

The Academy also specifies that certain alternative or modified test formats are not accepted.

The following are not accepted:

  • TOEFL MyBest Scores
  • TOEFL iBT Home Edition
  • IELTS Indicator
  • IELTS Online
  • IELTS One Skill Retake

Applicants should make sure that their English test meets the Academy’s accepted format and validity requirements.

How English Test Scores Must Be Submitted

For IELTS, TOEFL and Cambridge English tests, applicants cannot simply rely on uploading a copy of their score report where the Academy requires scores to be sent directly.

The Academy states that these scores must be sent directly by the relevant testing organizations.

When registering for the examination, applicants should select Yenching Academy of Peking University as the designated recipient of their scores.

For TOEFL applicants, the institution code is:

C488

Applicants should arrange this early enough to ensure that their scores reach the Academy before the application deadline.

Application Materials

Applicants are required to submit several materials through the Yenching Academy’s online application portal.

The application must be completed in English.

Required materials include:

  1. Completed online application form
  2. Personal statement of no more than 750 words
  3. Statement of Research Interest of no more than 1,500 words, excluding citations
  4. Curriculum Vitae
  5. Official transcript or transcripts
  6. Diploma or Certificate of Enrollment
  7. Two academic letters of recommendation
  8. Required English proficiency evidence, where applicable

Each component serves a different purpose in demonstrating the applicant’s academic preparation, research interests, leadership potential and suitability for the programme.

Personal Statement

The personal statement must be 750 words or less.

This is an opportunity for applicants to present their background and explain why they are suitable candidates for the Yenching Academy.

Rather than simply repeating information already available in the CV, applicants should use the statement to provide context around their academic journey, interests, achievements and motivation.

A strong personal statement should help admissions reviewers understand the applicant as a person and explain why the Yenching Academy is an appropriate next step.

Statement of Research Interest

Applicants must also submit a Statement of Research Interest of no more than 1,500 words, excluding citations.

This is particularly important because the Yenching Academy emphasizes interdisciplinary study of China.

Applicants should use the statement to explain the research questions or areas they are interested in exploring and demonstrate their intellectual engagement with issues concerning China.

The statement should be focused, coherent and academically grounded.

Applicants should avoid treating the statement as a generic essay about why they want to study in China. Instead, they should clearly communicate their research interests and explain the issues they would like to investigate.

Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must submit a Curriculum Vitae.

The CV should provide a clear overview of the applicant’s:

  • Academic background
  • Research experience
  • Professional experience, where applicable
  • Leadership activities
  • Extracurricular achievements
  • Community engagement
  • Relevant projects
  • Awards and accomplishments

Because the Academy specifically values extracurricular achievement, social responsibility and leadership potential, applicants should ensure that their CV captures relevant activities beyond academic qualifications.

Academic Transcripts

Applicants must provide official transcript(s).

The transcripts allow the Academy to assess the applicant’s academic record and verify educational performance.

Applicants should ensure that their academic documents are official and complete and that any required translation or certification requirements are satisfied where applicable.

Diploma or Certificate of Enrollment

Applicants must also submit the appropriate educational-status documentation.

This may be:

  • A diploma demonstrating completion of a Bachelor’s degree; or
  • A Certificate of Enrollment for applicants who are still completing their Bachelor’s programme.

Students who are currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s programme must expect to receive their diploma by August of the intended enrollment year.

Academic Recommendation Letters

Applicants must provide two academic letters of recommendation.

The recommendation letters may be written in:

  • Chinese; or
  • English.

However, the Academy imposes specific requirements concerning who may write these letters.

Peking University will only accept recommendation letters written by:

  • Full professors; or
  • Associate professors; or
  • Individuals holding equivalent academic titles.

In addition, the recommendation letters must be submitted by professors in the applicant’s intended field of study.

Applicants should therefore select their referees carefully.

A recommendation from an individual who does not meet the specified academic rank or who is not connected to the applicant’s intended field may not satisfy the Academy’s requirements.

International Student Eligibility

For the 2027 cohort, international applicants must be non-Chinese citizens with a valid passport.

This is an important nationality requirement for candidates applying through the international admissions route.

Former citizens of the Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan who have emigrated to another country and are applying to Peking University as international students have additional documentation requirements.

They must provide:

  • Valid passport or citizenship documents dating from before April 30, 2021; and
  • Proof of cancellation of Chinese nationality.

Applicants with complicated nationality or citizenship histories should carefully consult Peking University’s international student admissions information before submitting an application.

Applicants from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan

Candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions have a separate application process.

Applications for the 2027 Yenching Scholars cohort open on:

September 1, 2026

The deadline is:

November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time

Candidates from these regions must apply through the Yenching Academy application portal and also complete a supplementary application through the Peking University Graduate Admissions website.

Additional information is provided through Peking University’s admissions resources.

Applicants from the Chinese Mainland

The application process for candidates from the Chinese Mainland is handled through the relevant Peking University graduate admissions system.

The Academy directs Mainland Chinese candidates to the Graduate School of Peking University for additional information about the application process.

Applicants from the Chinese Mainland should therefore carefully follow the specific admissions instructions applicable to their applicant category rather than assuming that the international application procedure applies to them.

Learn More HERE

Partner University Applicants

Students and alumni of Yenching Academy’s Partner Universities must complete their home university’s internal pre-selection process before submitting an application to the Yenching Academy.

This is a particularly important requirement for candidates associated with partner institutions.

Applicants should therefore determine whether their university is included among the Academy’s partner universities and, if it is, find out whether their university has an internal nomination or pre-selection process.

Waiting until the Yenching Academy application deadline may be too late if the applicant’s university has an earlier internal deadline.

Application Portal

Candidates can submit their applications through the Yenching Academy’s online application portal.

Applicants are required to create an account before accessing additional application information and submitting their materials.

The application portal is also where applicants can find further instructions concerning the admissions process.

Applicants should make sure that all information entered into the portal is accurate and consistent with the supporting documents they submit.

APPLY HERE

Important Rule Regarding Other Degree Programmes

Peking University does not allow students to be enrolled in another degree programme while studying at the university.

Applicants who are currently enrolled in another degree programme should therefore consider this rule when planning their studies.

They should review their existing academic commitments and ensure that they understand Peking University’s requirements before accepting an offer.

Fellowship Benefits

The Yenching Academy provides a comprehensive fellowship package to all scholars.

The fellowship includes five major forms of support.

Tuition Fees

Selected scholars receive coverage of tuition fees.

This removes one of the major financial costs associated with pursuing graduate education.

Accommodation

The fellowship also provides accommodation.

This is particularly valuable for international students relocating to Beijing because housing can represent a significant component of the overall cost of studying abroad.

Monthly Stipend

Scholars receive a monthly stipend.

The supplied programme information does not specify the exact amount of the monthly stipend, so applicants should consult the admissions portal or official programme information for the current figure.

One Round-Trip Travel Fare

The fellowship includes one round-trip travel fare.

This provides travel support for the scholar and can help reduce the cost associated with travelling to and from Beijing.

Field Study Costs

The fellowship also covers field study costs.

This component is particularly relevant to the Academy’s interdisciplinary approach, as field-based academic experiences can provide scholars with opportunities to deepen their understanding of China beyond classroom-based study.

Why Study at Yenching Academy?

The Yenching Academy offers more than financial support.

Its structure is particularly suited to students who want to develop a deeper understanding of China through interdisciplinary academic inquiry.

Several characteristics make the programme distinctive.

Interdisciplinary Academic Environment

Students can explore China through different academic perspectives rather than being limited to a single disciplinary framework.

This can be particularly beneficial for students interested in complex issues that cross traditional academic boundaries.

International Community

With international students making up approximately 75 percent of the student body, the Academy provides a highly international learning environment.

Students can interact with peers from different countries and backgrounds while developing a deeper understanding of China.

Leadership Development

The Academy looks for applicants with leadership potential, community engagement and social responsibility.

This creates an environment where academic development can be combined with broader leadership and social-impact interests.

Research Opportunities

The requirement for a Statement of Research Interest highlights the programme’s emphasis on intellectual inquiry.

Students with clearly developed research interests can use the programme to investigate questions relating to China from an interdisciplinary perspective.

Field Study

The fellowship’s inclusion of field study costs provides scholars with financial support for field-based academic activities.

Such experiences can complement classroom learning and help scholars connect academic concepts with real-world contexts.

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

Because the Yenching Academy attracts high-achieving candidates, applicants should begin preparing well before the deadline.

Start With Eligibility

First, confirm that you meet the fundamental requirements.

Check:

  • Your Bachelor’s degree status
  • Your expected graduation date if you are still an undergraduate
  • Your academic record
  • Your interest in interdisciplinary study of China
  • Your extracurricular and leadership experience
  • Your English proficiency
  • Your nationality and applicant category

Develop a Clear Research Interest

The Statement of Research Interest is one of the most important components of the application.

Applicants should spend sufficient time identifying a focused area of inquiry.

Rather than selecting an extremely broad topic, consider a specific question or problem related to China that can be examined through an interdisciplinary perspective.

Choose Recommendation Writers Early

Because recommendation letters must come from full professors, associate professors or equivalent academic titles and should be from professors in the intended field of study, applicants should approach potential referees early.

This is especially important because academic referees may have multiple commitments and may require considerable time to prepare a thoughtful recommendation.

Prepare English Test Scores Early

Applicants who require an English proficiency test should avoid waiting until immediately before the deadline.

The Academy requires eligible English tests to have been taken after September 1, 2025 and does not accept several alternative test formats.

Applicants should also allow sufficient time for scores to be sent directly from the testing organization to Yenching Academy.

Review Every Document

Before submitting the application, applicants should ensure that:

  • Names are consistent across documents.
  • Academic dates are accurate.
  • Transcripts are official.
  • Recommendation letters meet the academic-rank requirements.
  • The personal statement does not exceed 750 words.
  • The Statement of Research Interest does not exceed 1,500 words excluding citations.
  • The CV is complete and professionally presented.
  • English test scores meet the required minimum where applicable.
  • Required documents have been submitted in the correct format.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the 2027 Yenching Scholars cohort for international candidates and candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions is:

November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time.

Applications open on September 1, 2026.

Applicants should not wait until the final day to submit their applications because the process involves multiple supporting documents and, for some candidates, university-level pre-selection procedures.

Important Application Considerations

Applicants should keep several requirements in mind when preparing their applications.

First, students and alumni of Partner Universities must complete their university’s internal pre-selection process before submitting their Yenching Academy application.

Second, applicants who need English proficiency tests must ensure that their test was taken after September 1, 2025 and that the examination format is accepted.

Third, international candidates must satisfy the nationality requirements for international admission.

Finally, applicants should carefully follow any additional instructions displayed in the admissions portal after creating an account.
