Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Yenching Academy Scholarship?

The Yenching Academy provides a generous fellowship to students admitted to its interdisciplinary graduate programme at Peking University. The fellowship includes tuition fees, accommodation, a monthly stipend, one round-trip travel fare and field study costs.

Is the Yenching Academy programme open to international students?

Yes. International students make up approximately 75 percent of the Yenching Academy student body. For the international admissions route, applicants must be non-Chinese citizens with a valid passport.

What degree do I need to apply?

Applicants need at least a Bachelor’s degree in any field or must currently be enrolled in a Bachelor’s programme and expect to receive their diploma by August of the intended enrollment year.

Can students from any Bachelor’s field apply?

Yes. The Academy states that applicants may hold a Bachelor’s degree in any field.

Do I need to demonstrate leadership experience?

The Academy seeks applicants with a record of extracurricular achievement, community engagement, social responsibility and leadership potential. Applicants should therefore demonstrate meaningful involvement and evidence of initiative.

What is the English requirement?

Accepted minimum scores include IELTS Academic 7.0, TOEFL iBT 100, Cambridge English Scale 185, CET 6 600 or TEM 4 at the required “良好” or above level.

Are English tests required for everyone?

No. International applicants whose native language is English or who have graduated from an English-taught degree programme at undergraduate level or above do not need to provide an English proficiency test report. However, applicants from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan must provide one even if their degree was taught in English.

How many recommendation letters are required?

Two academic recommendation letters are required.

Who can write the recommendation letters?

Letters must be written by full professors, associate professors or individuals with equivalent academic titles, and they must come from professors in the applicant’s intended field of study.

How much is the monthly stipend?

The supplied programme information confirms that a monthly stipend is provided but does not specify the amount. Applicants should check the admissions portal for the current stipend amount.

Does the fellowship cover tuition?

Yes. Tuition fees are included in the fellowship.

Does the fellowship cover accommodation?

Yes. Accommodation is included.

Does the fellowship include travel support?

Yes. The fellowship includes one round-trip travel fare.

Does it cover field study?

Yes. Field study costs are included in the fellowship.

When does the 2027 application open?

Applications for international candidates and candidates from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan open on September 1, 2026.

When is the application deadline?

The deadline is November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time.

Can students from Partner Universities apply directly?

Students and alumni of Partner Universities must first complete their home university’s internal pre-selection process before submitting the Yenching Academy application.

Can international students who were previously Chinese citizens apply?

Potentially, but additional documentation requirements apply. Former citizens of the Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan who have emigrated to other countries must provide qualifying passport or citizenship documents dating from before April 30, 2021, together with proof of cancellation of Chinese nationality.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Yenching Academy of Peking University Scholarship 2027.

Conclusion

The Yenching Academy of Peking University Scholarship 2027 is a highly attractive opportunity for academically outstanding students who want to pursue an interdisciplinary graduate education focused on China in an international academic environment.

The programme combines rigorous academic study with an internationally diverse student community and places considerable emphasis on intellectual curiosity, leadership potential, community engagement and social responsibility.

For successful scholars, the financial package is particularly significant. The Yenching Academy provides tuition fees, accommodation, a monthly stipend, one round-trip travel fare and field study costs, allowing selected students to undertake their studies with substantial financial support.

Applicants should nevertheless recognize that this is a competitive programme. A strong application should go beyond meeting the minimum eligibility requirements. Candidates should present an outstanding academic record, demonstrate meaningful extracurricular and community engagement, articulate a convincing interest in the interdisciplinary study of China and submit carefully prepared application materials.

For international candidates and candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions, applications for the 2027 cohort open on September 1, 2026, and the application deadline is November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time.

Prospective applicants should begin preparing their transcripts, CV, personal statement, research-interest statement, recommendation letters and English-language documentation well in advance. Candidates from Partner Universities should also investigate their institution’s internal pre-selection deadline because this process must be completed before submitting the Yenching Academy application.

Overall, the Yenching Academy provides an opportunity for talented students from diverse academic and geographic backgrounds to study at Peking University, deepen their understanding of China and develop an international network while receiving substantial fellowship support.

For the latest application instructions and to begin the application process, prospective candidates should consult the official Yenching Academy admissions portal.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026, an exciting opportunity designed to recognise and support young South Africans who are actively contributing to positive change in their communities and across the country.

Offered through a partnership between Brand South Africa and One Young World, the Play Your Part Bursary will enable six outstanding young South Africans to participate in the One Young World Summit 2026, taking place in Cape Town, South Africa, from 3–6 November 2026.

The opportunity is specifically aimed at young active citizens who are already making meaningful contributions to South African society. Successful candidates will have the opportunity to participate in one of the world’s prominent gatherings of emerging young leaders, engage with a diverse leadership community and gain access to development opportunities that extend beyond the Summit itself.

Applications opened on 11 August 2026 and interested candidates must submit their applications by 16 September 2026.

About the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026

The Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026 has been created to support young South Africans who demonstrate the values of active citizenship through tangible contributions to their communities and society.

The bursary is connected to Brand South Africa’s wider mission of strengthening the country’s reputation, competitiveness and sense of national participation.

Brand South Africa is the official marketing agency of South Africa. Its mandate includes building South Africa’s brand reputation and improving the country’s global competitiveness.

Through coordinated and proactive marketing and communications strategies, the organisation works to position South Africa as a competitive investment destination while simultaneously encouraging South Africans, both within the country and abroad, to participate actively in building a better society.

A central part of this work is the Play Your Part initiative.

What Is the Play Your Part Initiative?

Play Your Part is a nationwide initiative developed to inspire, empower and celebrate active citizenship in South Africa.

The initiative is based on the principle that building a stronger country is a collective responsibility and that contributions to society can take many different forms.

Rather than limiting active citizenship to formal organisations or large-scale projects, Play Your Part encourages participation from across South African society, including:

  • Individuals;
  • Businesses and corporations;
  • Non-governmental organisations;
  • Government institutions;
  • Schools;
  • Faith communities; and
  • Other community groups and organisations.

Participants are encouraged to contribute whatever resources they can towards creating a better future. Contributions may include their:

  • Time;
  • Money;
  • Professional or personal skills;
  • Knowledge;
  • Resources; or
  • Goods.

At its core, Play Your Part seeks to demonstrate the impact that can be achieved when people actively care for their communities, fellow citizens and the environment.

The partnership with One Young World extends this mission by identifying young people who are already putting these principles into practice and providing them with an international leadership development opportunity.

Six Young South Africans Will Receive the Bursary

A total of six bursaries are available through the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026.

The bursaries have been divided geographically to ensure opportunities for both Cape Town-based candidates and young leaders elsewhere in South Africa.

The six places are allocated as follows:

  • Three bursaries are reserved for candidates based in Cape Town.
  • Three bursaries are available to applicants from across South Africa.

Successful candidates will participate in the One Young World Summit 2026 alongside other emerging leaders and changemakers.

About the One Young World Summit 2026

The One Young World Summit 2026 will take place from 3–6 November 2026 in Cape Town, South Africa.

The Summit brings together young leaders and provides a platform for participants to connect, exchange ideas, discuss important global and local challenges, and strengthen their capacity to create positive change.

For recipients of the Play Your Part Bursary, participation is intended to be more than attendance at a single event. Successful applicants will also gain access to leadership development opportunities and the wider One Young World community.

This makes the bursary particularly relevant to young South Africans who are already demonstrating leadership through community service, social initiatives, civic participation or other activities that benefit society.

What Does the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary Cover?

Successful applicants will receive support to participate in the One Young World Summit 2026.

The bursary includes the following:

1. Access to the One Young World Summit 2026

Recipients will receive access to the One Young World Summit 2026, scheduled for 3–6 November 2026 in Cape Town, South Africa.

This gives successful candidates the opportunity to participate in the Summit’s activities and engage with the wider One Young World community.

2. Travel and Accommodation Where Required

The bursary provides travel and accommodation as required for eligible successful candidates.

However, an important exception applies to applicants who are already based in Cape Town.

Travel and accommodation will not be provided for candidates based in Cape Town.

Applicants should therefore take this condition into consideration when applying.

3. Catering During the Summit

Selected participants will receive catering during specified periods of the Summit.

The package includes:

  • Dinner on 3 November 2026;
  • Lunch and dinner on 4 November 2026;
  • Lunch and dinner on 5 November 2026; and
  • Lunch and dinner on 6 November 2026.

4. Access to the One Young World Global Leadership Programme

Bursary recipients will also receive access to the One Young World Global Leadership Programme.

This component adds a leadership development dimension to the opportunity and is particularly relevant to candidates seeking to strengthen their ability to contribute effectively to their communities and wider society.

5. Access to Action Accelerator

Successful candidates will receive access to Action Accelerator, a One Young World programme connected to supporting leadership and action.

For young people already developing initiatives or contributing to community projects, this provides an additional opportunity to build on the work they are currently undertaking.

6. Lifetime Membership of the One Young World Ambassador Community

One of the longer-term benefits of the bursary is lifetime membership in the One Young World Ambassador Community.

This means that the value of the opportunity extends beyond the four-day Summit in Cape Town.

Successful participants will become part of the wider One Young World community after the Summit, creating opportunities for continued engagement with other young leaders and changemakers.

Who Is Eligible for the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026?

The bursary has specific eligibility requirements, and candidates should review them carefully before submitting an application.

Age Requirement

Candidates must be between 18 and 30 years old at the time of the One Young World Summit 2026.

Applicants who will still be under the age of 18 at the time of the Summit cannot be accepted.

Candidates should therefore calculate their age based on the Summit dates rather than only their age at the time they submit their application.

Nationality or Residency Requirement

Applicants must be a:

  • South African national; or
  • Resident of South Africa.

The opportunity is therefore specifically focused on young people connected to South Africa through nationality or residency.

Commitment to Active Citizenship

Candidates must demonstrate a genuine commitment to active citizenship and contributing to positive change in South Africa.

The bursary is not simply based on academic qualifications or professional achievements. Applicants are expected to demonstrate that they are already actively contributing to their communities or society.

Evidence of Community or Social Contribution

Applicants should be able to demonstrate a track record of using one or more of the following to benefit their community or society:

  • Time;
  • Money;
  • Skills; or
  • Goods.

This requirement reflects the philosophy behind the Play Your Part initiative: positive change can come from different forms of contribution.

Applicants should therefore consider the practical impact they have already made and how their actions have benefited other people, their community or South African society more broadly.

Understanding of Issues Affecting South Africa

Candidates must demonstrate an understanding of key local and/or global issues facing South Africa.

This means applicants should be able to connect their active citizenship or community involvement to broader challenges and opportunities affecting the country.

What Type of Candidate Is the Bursary Looking For?

The Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary is particularly suited to young people who are not simply interested in leadership as a concept but are already demonstrating it through action.

Strong applicants are likely to be able to show clear evidence of how they have contributed to positive change.

This contribution could potentially take different forms, provided it demonstrates the required commitment to active citizenship.

Applicants should therefore think carefully about questions such as:

  1. What have I personally done to contribute to positive change?
  2. Who has benefited from my actions?
  3. What problem or social challenge have I attempted to address?
  4. What resources, skills, time or goods have I contributed?
  5. What measurable or meaningful difference has my contribution made?
  6. What important issues affecting South Africa do I understand particularly well?
  7. How could participation in the One Young World Summit strengthen my ability to continue creating positive change?

Candidates who can communicate their answers clearly may be better positioned to demonstrate alignment with the purpose of the bursary.

Why Young South African Changemakers Should Consider Applying

The Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary offers more than access to an international leadership gathering.

It creates an opportunity for young South Africans already contributing to their communities to expand their leadership exposure and become part of a wider community.

For successful applicants, the opportunity includes:

  • Participation in the One Young World Summit 2026;
  • Exposure to a wider community of young leaders;
  • Access to leadership development programming;
  • Participation in Action Accelerator;
  • Lifetime membership of the One Young World Ambassador Community;
  • Travel and accommodation support where applicable; and
  • An opportunity to represent the spirit of active citizenship in South Africa.

The bursary may therefore be especially valuable for community leaders, social changemakers and other young people who are already turning ideas into meaningful action.

Important Dates for Applicants

Prospective applicants should take note of the following dates:

  • Applications opened: 11 August 2026
  • Application deadline: 16 September 2026
  • One Young World Summit: 3–6 November 2026
  • Summit location: Cape Town, South Africa

Applicants are encouraged not to wait until the final day to prepare and submit their applications.

Application Deadline

The official application deadline for the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026 is 16 September 2026.

Applications submitted after the stated deadline may not be considered, so prospective candidates should ensure that they complete the application process on time.

How to Apply for the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026

Interested candidates should apply through the official One Young World application portal for the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary.

Before starting the application, candidates should carefully review the eligibility criteria and think about how they will demonstrate their record of active citizenship.

Applicants should be prepared to communicate clearly:

  • Their commitment to positive change in South Africa;
  • Their record of contributing time, money, skills or goods;
  • The impact of their activities on their community or wider society;
  • Their understanding of issues affecting South Africa; and
  • How their experiences align with the values of the Play Your Part initiative.

Official opportunity page:
https://www.oneyoungworld.com/scholarship/brand-south-africa-play-your-part-bursary

Application portal:
https://apply.oneyoungworld.com/scholarship/form/brand-south-africa-play-your-par

Candidates interested in learning more about Brand South Africa can also visit:

https://www.brandsouthafrica.com/

Important Note for Cape Town Applicants

Applicants based in Cape Town should pay particular attention to the funding arrangements.

Three of the six bursaries are specifically reserved for candidates based in Cape Town. However, travel and accommodation are not provided for Cape Town-based candidates.

The remaining three bursaries are open to applicants from across South Africa, with travel and accommodation provided as required.

Candidates should understand these arrangements before submitting their application.

Conclusion

The Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026 provides an important opportunity for young South Africans who are already demonstrating that active citizenship can create meaningful change.

Through the partnership between Brand South Africa and One Young World, six young people will be selected to participate in the One Young World Summit 2026 in Cape Town from 3–6 November 2026.

Beyond access to the Summit, successful candidates will benefit from leadership development opportunities, Action Accelerator and lifetime membership in the One Young World Ambassador Community. Travel and accommodation will also be supported where required, although this support does not apply to successful candidates based in Cape Town.

Most importantly, this opportunity is designed for young people who can demonstrate action. Applicants should have a track record of contributing their time, money, skills or goods towards improving their communities or society and should understand important issues affecting South Africa.

Young South African citizens and residents aged 18–30 who meet the criteria and are actively contributing to positive change are encouraged to consider applying.

Applications close on 16 September 2026.

Interested candidates should review the official requirements carefully and submit their applications through the One Young World application platform before the deadline.

Visit the OFY website for more Scholarship Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
Orr Fellowship 2027 offers ambitious college graduates and early-career professionals looking for more than a traditional entry-level position the opportunity to combine full-time professional employment with structured leadership development, mentorship, business training and access to an established professional community.

Applications are now open for the 2027 Orr Fellowship cohort, a two-year corporate fellowship programme designed to connect high-achieving college graduates with meaningful roles at innovative partner companies in Indiana. Successful Fellows gain real-world professional experience while participating in intentional career and leadership development designed to accelerate their transition from college into the workplace.

Fellows can be placed with partner companies in either Indianapolis or Evansville, Indiana, where they work full-time while becoming part of the wider Orr Fellowship community. The programme provides exposure to industries including technology, healthcare, finance, consulting, marketing and operations, with partner organisations ranging from high-growth startups to established companies.

The application deadline for the 2027 cohort is September 25 at 11:59 p.m.

What Is the Orr Fellowship?

Orr Fellowship is a two-year corporate fellowship programme created for high-achieving college graduates and young professionals preparing to begin their careers.

Rather than separating professional development from employment, Orr Fellowship combines the two. Fellows are matched with partner companies where they take on full-time roles and gain practical workplace experience from the beginning of the programme.

At the same time, Fellows participate in structured professional and leadership development activities that complement their responsibilities at their partner companies.

The programme is therefore designed for graduates who want to begin building a professional career while receiving additional training, mentorship, networking opportunities and exposure to business leaders.

According to Orr Fellowship, participants receive two years of full-time, on-the-job experience alongside professional and leadership development.

Why Consider the Orr Fellowship 2027?

Starting a career after college can involve more than simply securing a first job. New graduates may also need to develop professional networks, learn how organisations operate, strengthen communication skills, understand different career pathways and determine where their strengths can create the greatest impact.

Orr Fellowship is structured to help participants navigate this transition.

Fellows receive opportunities for:

  • Full-time professional employment and real-world work experience.
  • Leadership and career development.
  • Business and communication skills development.
  • Workshops and speaker series.
  • Mentorship.
  • Cohort-based learning.
  • Exposure to executives and business leaders.
  • Connections with peers and Orr Fellowship alumni.
  • Experience working across teams and business functions.
  • Long-term professional networking.

The combination of employment and structured development is one of the programme’s defining features.

Two Years of Full-Time Professional Experience

Orr Fellows are not simply attending workshops or participating in a short-term training programme.

They work in full-time roles with Orr Fellowship partner companies.

Fellows may be placed across numerous industries and professional functions depending on partner-company needs and the Fellow’s skills and strengths. The Fellowship specifically highlights opportunities across fields such as:

  • Technology
  • Healthcare
  • Finance
  • Consulting
  • Marketing
  • Operations

The partner network includes both high-growth startups and more established organisations.

This gives Fellows an opportunity to develop practical skills within real organisations while simultaneously building their broader professional capabilities.

Hiring, Compensation and Benefits

Successful Orr Fellows are hired as full-time employees by their partner companies.

They receive competitive compensation and employee benefits aligned with entry-level employment while contributing to meaningful professional work.

This distinction is important for prospective applicants: Orr Fellowship provides a structured development experience alongside actual full-time employment rather than functioning solely as an academic or classroom-based fellowship.

The Fellow’s work at their partner company provides the practical component of the experience, while Orr Fellowship programming supports broader professional growth.

Professional and Leadership Development

The Orr Fellowship programme is intentionally designed to complement each Fellow’s full-time position.

Development programming focuses on areas such as:

  • Leadership development
  • Career development
  • Business skills
  • Communication skills
  • Executive exposure
  • Cross-functional exposure

Programming takes place during dedicated development days or outside core working hours, allowing Fellows to continue fulfilling their responsibilities as full-time employees.

Fellows can also access ongoing training through workshops, speaker series, mentorship and cohort-based learning.

The intention is to develop capabilities that extend beyond the Fellow’s immediate job description and can continue benefiting them throughout their careers.

Mentorship and Ongoing Support

Another major component of the Fellowship is the support available throughout the two-year experience.

Early-career professionals can encounter challenges ranging from adjusting to professional environments to determining career direction and building confidence in communicating with senior colleagues.

Orr Fellowship provides participants with mentorship, structured programming and a peer community that can help them navigate these early-career experiences.

If questions or challenges arise during the Fellowship, Orr also serves as a resource for Fellows and partner companies.

This support structure means Fellows have access not only to their employer but also to the wider Orr Fellowship ecosystem throughout the programme.

Build a Professional Network Early in Your Career

Professional relationships can play an important role in long-term career development, and networking is incorporated into the Orr Fellowship experience.

Fellows can build relationships with:

  • Other members of their cohort
  • Fellows from other cohorts
  • Orr Fellowship alumni
  • Mentors
  • Business leaders
  • Executives
  • Partner-company representatives
  • Professionals across different industries

The programme specifically highlights access to a network of peers, alumni and business leaders as one of the experiences available to Fellows.

After completing the two-year programme, Fellows become part of the Orr Fellowship alumni network, extending the community beyond the formal Fellowship period.

Who Can Apply for the Orr Fellowship 2027?

Orr Fellowship welcomes applicants from a wide range of academic backgrounds.

Importantly, applicants are not required to have completed a particular major or degree discipline. The programme states that Fellows come from diverse academic fields and are connected by qualities such as drive, curiosity and leadership potential.

Strong candidates typically demonstrate:

  • Interest in professional and leadership development.
  • Previous internship experience.
  • Campus, extracurricular or other relevant work experience.
  • Leadership involvement in academic, professional or community settings.
  • Strong potential to contribute within a professional environment.
  • A willingness to live in Indiana.
  • U.S. work authorisation.

The programme also identifies a GPA of 3.2 or above as typical among strong candidates. However, applications are reviewed holistically, and flexibility may be considered.

This means applicants should consider their complete profile rather than assuming that one individual factor automatically determines their chances.

Do You Need a Specific College Major?

No specific major is required.

This makes the Orr Fellowship relevant to graduates from a variety of academic disciplines rather than limiting participation to business, entrepreneurship or another particular field.

Applicants should instead consider how their experiences demonstrate leadership potential, curiosity, initiative, professional readiness and a desire to develop.

U.S. Work Authorisation Requirement

Prospective applicants should pay particular attention to the employment eligibility requirement.

Strong candidates are expected to have U.S. work authorisation and be willing to live in Indiana.

Because Fellows become full-time employees of partner companies, applicants should ensure they meet the programme’s work-authorisation requirements before applying.

Orr Fellowship Locations: Indianapolis and Evansville

Applicants can pursue the Fellowship through two Indiana chapters:

Indianapolis Chapter

The Indianapolis chapter is positioned for candidates interested in beginning their careers in a larger market.

It offers access to expansive professional networks, diverse roles and longer-term opportunities across industries.

Evansville Chapter

The Evansville chapter provides the same core Fellowship programming while offering the experience of developing professionally within a smaller market.

The programme highlights meaningful impact, leadership visibility and a strong regional identity among the characteristics of the Evansville experience.

Both chapters provide the same core professional-development experience. The primary differences relate to location, community size and local industry presence.

How the Orr Fellowship Recruitment Process Works

Candidates should be prepared for a structured recruitment and matching process rather than a single application followed immediately by an employment decision.

Recruitment generally takes place from August through December and involves a four-stage process incorporating:

  1. Application
  2. Interviewing
  3. Networking
  4. Final placement

Throughout the process, candidates may interact with Orr Fellowship alumni, partner organisations and other applicants.

The process is designed not simply to select applicants but also to match candidates with partner organisations where their skills and strengths align with hiring needs.

How the Company Matching Process Works

Orr Fellowship uses a mutual matching process between candidates and participating companies.

At Finalist Day, candidates may interview with multiple partner companies whose recruitment needs align with their skills and strengths.

Many candidates may receive offers on Finalist Day, although placements can continue afterward.

The Fellowship also notes that, in certain circumstances, a candidate may be placed directly within a partner company as an Orr Fellow instead of proceeding through the traditional selection process. Such placements depend on candidate qualifications and company needs.

Candidates are typically informed about their next steps within a few weeks following each stage.

What Do You Need to Apply?

The initial application requirements are relatively straightforward.

According to the programme’s application information, candidates need:

  • A resume.
  • Basic personal information.

These materials are required to get the application process started.

Applicants should nevertheless take time to prepare a strong resume that clearly demonstrates relevant internships, work experience, campus involvement, extracurricular activities, leadership responsibilities and other experiences that demonstrate their professional potential.

Application Deadline for the Orr Fellowship 2027

Deadline: September 25 at 11:59 p.m.

The Orr Fellowship application page states that applications for the 2027 cohort close September 25 at 11:59 p.m.

Prospective candidates should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their application. Applying early provides additional time to review application information, prepare a polished resume and address any technical issues that could arise during submission.

How to Apply for the Orr Fellowship 2027

Applicants can apply separately depending on which Orr Fellowship chapter they wish to pursue.

The official application page provides application routes for:

  • Indianapolis
  • Evansville

Candidates should first review the programme requirements and determine which location best aligns with their professional and personal goals.

The official Orr Fellowship application page is available through the programme’s website under Apply to Orr Fellowship.

Applicants who are interested in more than one chapter should carefully review the programme’s chapter information and application instructions.

APPLY NOW

Not Ready to Apply Yet?

Students who are interested in Orr Fellowship but are not yet ready or eligible to join can remain connected with the organisation.

The Fellowship specifically encourages sophomores, juniors and other future candidates to request additional information.

By doing so, prospective future applicants can:

  • Receive programme updates.
  • Learn about future application deadlines.
  • Hear from current Fellows and alumni.
  • Remain informed until they become eligible to apply.

This can be particularly useful for students who want to use their remaining time at university to strengthen their internship experience, leadership involvement and professional profile.

Why the Orr Fellowship Can Be Valuable for Early-Career Professionals

The Orr Fellowship is particularly notable because it brings together several aspects of early-career development within one two-year experience.

Participants are able to build their careers through real employment, rather than relying exclusively on simulated business exercises or classroom learning. At the same time, their employment is supplemented by structured development opportunities that may help broaden their professional perspective.

For graduates who want exposure beyond the responsibilities of a single entry-level position, the programme offers opportunities to learn from business leaders, engage with peers, strengthen leadership and communication capabilities and build a professional network early in their careers.

The Fellowship can therefore appeal to applicants who want both immediate professional responsibility and a wider framework for long-term career development.

Conclusion

The Orr Fellowship 2027 offers high-achieving college graduates and young professionals an opportunity to launch their careers through a combination of full-time employment, two years of professional experience, leadership development, mentorship, business training and community.

Successful Fellows work as full-time employees at partner companies in Indianapolis or Evansville, Indiana, while participating in structured programming designed to strengthen leadership, career, business and communication capabilities.

With opportunities spanning industries such as technology, healthcare, finance, consulting, marketing and operations, the programme is open to applicants from diverse academic disciplines. Candidates are evaluated holistically, although strong applicants typically bring internship or extracurricular experience, leadership involvement, professional-development ambitions and a GPA around 3.2 or higher. Applicants must also have U.S. work authorisation and be willing to live in Indiana.

For college graduates seeking an entry point into meaningful professional work while developing a strong network and leadership foundation, the Orr Fellowship provides a structured pathway from university into the professional world.

item.content:encoded:
Young South African entrepreneurs with businesses capable of creating significant employment opportunities have an opportunity to connect with a global network of young leaders through the One Young World National Programme for Job-Generating Entrepreneurs 2026.

The programme has been created as part of One Young World’s wider commitment to addressing one of South Africa’s most pressing challenges: youth unemployment. It seeks to identify and support young entrepreneurs who are not only building businesses but are also creating pathways to employment and livelihoods for other young people.

Applications for the programme opened on 11 August 2026, and the application deadline is 12 September 2026.

Selected participants will have the opportunity to join the global One Young World community and participate in the One Young World Summit in Cape Town, South Africa, from 3–6 November 2026.

About the One Young World National Programme for Job-Generating Entrepreneurs

The National Programme for Job-Generating Entrepreneurs has been developed in connection with the One Young World Summit taking place in Cape Town.

One Young World describes the programme as part of a legacy commitment designed to respond to youth unemployment in South Africa through practical, business-led approaches to employment and job creation.

The programme recognises that young people are not only future employees. They can also be powerful creators of employment within their communities when they have the right businesses, networks, knowledge and opportunities to scale.

The initiative therefore focuses on entrepreneurs whose businesses have the potential to generate significant numbers of jobs and contribute meaningfully to economic opportunities for young people.

Rather than focusing solely on entrepreneurship as an individual career pathway, the programme places particular emphasis on entrepreneurs as job creators.

Why the Programme Was Created

Youth unemployment remains an important challenge in South Africa, and the programme aims to contribute to solutions that place young entrepreneurs at the centre of employment creation.

The information provided by One Young World highlights research indicating that 35% of young South Africans identify the creation of new, well-paying jobs as one of the most important steps Africa can take to progress. According to the programme information, this was the highest response among the 16 countries surveyed.

This finding reinforces the relevance of a programme focused on entrepreneurs who can create employment opportunities.

The One Young World Summit in Cape Town is therefore intended to be more than a global gathering. Through initiatives such as this programme, the Summit is also positioned as an opportunity to support practical solutions to national and regional challenges.

What the Programme Is Looking For

The programme is designed for young South African entrepreneurs who are actively leading businesses or enterprises and have the potential to create significant employment opportunities.

Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate that they are not simply interested in entrepreneurship but are already taking a leadership role within an organisation or business.

The programme specifically requires applicants to:

  • Lead a business or enterprise.
  • Have significant job-creation potential within their business.
  • Have direct decision-making authority within their organisation or company.
  • Be South African nationals and residents.
  • Meet the programme’s age requirements.
  • Be available to attend the One Young World Summit in Cape Town.

The focus on job creation makes this opportunity particularly relevant to entrepreneurs whose businesses are growing or have the potential to scale and employ more people.

Connection to the One Young World Global Community

One of the major aspects of the programme is its connection to the wider One Young World Ambassador Community.

Participants can become part of a global network of more than 20,000 young leaders across more than 190 countries.

This creates opportunities for young entrepreneurs to connect with individuals working on different social, economic and community challenges around the world.

Being part of such a network can expose participants to different approaches to entrepreneurship, employment creation, leadership and social impact.

The programme is therefore not only focused on the individual business of an entrepreneur. It also seeks to connect young business leaders with a broader international community of people working to create positive change.

Opportunities Available to Participants

The programme information states that participants will have access to several opportunities through their connection to One Young World.

These include:

1. Access to a Global Network

Participants will be connected to a global community of more than 20,000 young leaders from over 190 countries.

This international network brings together young people working across different sectors, industries and areas of social impact.

For entrepreneurs, such a network can provide exposure to new ideas, perspectives and potential professional relationships.

2. Ambassador Opportunities

Participants can gain access to exclusive opportunities available to One Young World Ambassadors.

These may include:

  • Speaking opportunities.
  • Regional networking opportunities.
  • Mentoring sessions.
  • Other engagement opportunities within the Ambassador Community.

These activities can support continued leadership development beyond the Summit itself.

3. Understanding the Youth Unemployment Challenge

The programme will also provide participants with an opportunity to improve their understanding of solutions to the youth unemployment crisis.

This is particularly relevant to entrepreneurs whose businesses already contribute to employment or have the potential to create additional jobs.

By engaging with other young leaders and the wider One Young World community, participants can explore different approaches to employment, entrepreneurship and economic participation.

4. Strengthening Enterprise Growth

Another important focus is increasing participants’ capacity to scale their enterprises as generators of employment opportunities.

The programme therefore connects entrepreneurship with the broader objective of creating sustainable jobs.

For a business leader, this can mean thinking beyond the survival of an individual enterprise and considering how business growth can translate into opportunities for other people.

One Young World Summit 2026 in Cape Town

Successful participants are expected to participate in the One Young World Summit in Cape Town, South Africa, from 3–6 November 2026.

The Summit provides an international platform where young leaders can connect, exchange ideas and engage with other people working on significant social and economic challenges.

For participants in the National Programme for Job-Generating Entrepreneurs, the Cape Town Summit will provide an opportunity to engage with a global leadership community while contributing perspectives from South Africa’s entrepreneurship and employment landscape.

The Summit is therefore a central component of the programme and applicants must be available to participate during the specified dates.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements before submitting an application.

To be eligible for the National Programme for Job-Generating Entrepreneurs, an applicant must:

  1. Be between 18 and 30 years of age.
  2. Be a national of South Africa and resident in South Africa.
  3. Be leading a business or enterprise with the potential for significant job creation.
  4. Have direct decision-making authority within their organisation or company.
  5. Be available to participate in the One Young World Summit from 3–6 November 2026.

Applicants Over 30

The programme notes that most delegates participating in the One Young World Summit are between 18 and 30.

However, applicants older than 30 may be considered where they can demonstrate appropriate levels of:

  • Personal impact.
  • Initiative.
  • Willingness to engage.

Applicants who will be under 18 at the time of the Summit, which takes place from 3–6 November 2026, cannot apply.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This programme may be particularly relevant to young South African entrepreneurs who are already running businesses and are interested in expanding their impact through employment creation.

Potential applicants could include entrepreneurs whose businesses operate in areas where growth can directly lead to new employment opportunities.

The key consideration is not simply having a business idea. The eligibility requirements specifically refer to applicants leading a business or enterprise that has the potential for significant job creation.

Applicants should therefore consider how their business contributes, or could contribute, to employment opportunities and economic participation.

The Importance of Direct Leadership

Another important eligibility requirement is that applicants must have direct decision-making authority within their organisation or company.

This means the opportunity is intended for entrepreneurs who have meaningful leadership responsibility rather than individuals who are simply employees or passive participants in a business.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate their role in making decisions and leading the organisation.

Nationality and Residency Requirement

The National Programme for Job-Generating Entrepreneurs is specifically focused on young entrepreneurs in South Africa.

Applicants must be both:

  • A national of South Africa; and
  • Resident in South Africa.

The opportunity information provided does not identify other countries as eligible.

Consequently, entrepreneurs from other African countries or other regions should not assume that they qualify for this particular national programme unless One Young World provides additional eligibility information.

Age Requirement

The standard age range for the programme is 18 to 30 years.

The programme does, however, allow for consideration of applicants over the age of 30 where there is evidence of appropriate personal impact, initiative and willingness to engage.

There is also a firm restriction concerning applicants under 18. The programme states that applications cannot be accepted from individuals who will be under 18 at the time of the One Young World Summit.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the National Programme for Job-Generating Entrepreneurs is:

12 September 2026

The application period opened on 11 August 2026.

Applicants should ensure that they submit their applications before the stated deadline and carefully review the official application requirements before completing their submission.

How to Apply

Applications are submitted through the official One Young World application platform.

Interested applicants should use the official application link provided on the programme page and complete the application process before the deadline.

Apply for the National Programme for Job-Generating Entrepreneurs

Applicants should ensure that the information they provide accurately reflects their entrepreneurial leadership, business activities and potential for job creation.

APPLY HERE.

Key Dates to Remember

The most important dates associated with the opportunity are:

  • Application opening date: 11 August 2026
  • Application deadline: 12 September 2026
  • One Young World Summit: 3–6 November 2026
  • Summit location: Cape Town, South Africa

Applicants should pay particular attention to the 12 September 2026 application deadline.

For more information, Visit HERE.

Why Job-Generating Entrepreneurs Matter

Entrepreneurship can play an important role in addressing unemployment by creating businesses that provide opportunities for other people.

A successful enterprise can generate direct employment while also supporting wider economic activity through suppliers, customers, service providers and other businesses.

The National Programme for Job-Generating Entrepreneurs reflects this approach by focusing on entrepreneurs who have the potential to create significant numbers of jobs.

The programme therefore places the entrepreneur within a wider economic and social context: building a business is not only about personal success but can also become a pathway to employment and livelihoods for others.

What Makes This Opportunity Different?

The programme stands out because of its specific focus on job-generating entrepreneurship.

While many entrepreneurship opportunities focus on developing business ideas, skills or individual enterprises, this initiative specifically seeks young entrepreneurs whose businesses can contribute to solving the employment challenge.

It also combines national entrepreneurship priorities with international leadership development through the One Young World network.

Participants can therefore connect a local challenge, namely youth unemployment in South Africa, with a global community of young leaders.

International Networking and Exposure

Joining the One Young World community can provide participants with an international perspective on leadership and social impact.

The network includes young leaders from more than 190 countries, creating an environment where participants can encounter different approaches to entrepreneurship, innovation, community development and employment creation.

For South African entrepreneurs, international exposure can also provide opportunities to learn from businesses and leaders working in different economic environments.

Leadership Development

The programme is also connected to One Young World’s wider focus on young leadership.

Through networking, speaking opportunities, mentoring and engagement with other Ambassadors, participants can continue developing their leadership capabilities.

The experience may be particularly valuable for entrepreneurs who want to strengthen their ability to lead organisations while increasing their social and economic impact.

What Entrepreneurs Should Highlight in Their Applications

Eligible entrepreneurs should ensure that their applications clearly communicate the aspects of their work that align with the programme’s objectives.

Important areas to demonstrate include:

  • The business or enterprise they lead.
  • Their role and decision-making authority.
  • The problem their business addresses.
  • Current or potential employment opportunities created by the business.
  • The potential for the enterprise to scale.
  • Their personal leadership and impact.
  • Their contribution to their community or wider society.
  • Their availability to participate in the One Young World Summit.

The strongest applications should make it clear how the applicant’s entrepreneurial work connects with the programme’s central focus on job creation.

Important Information for Prospective Applicants

Before applying, prospective candidates should carefully assess whether they meet the programme’s requirements.

In particular, applicants should confirm that they:

  • Are South African nationals.
  • Currently reside in South Africa.
  • Meet the age requirements.
  • Lead a business or enterprise.
  • Have direct decision-making authority.
  • Can demonstrate significant job-creation potential.
  • Can attend the One Young World Summit in Cape Town from 3–6 November 2026.

Meeting these requirements is important because the programme is specifically designed for young South African entrepreneurs who can contribute to the objective of creating employment opportunities.

Conclusion

The One Young World National Programme for Job-Generating Entrepreneurs 2026 provides a platform for young South African entrepreneurs whose businesses have the potential to create significant employment opportunities.

By connecting participants to the One Young World community of more than 20,000 young leaders across more than 190 countries, the programme provides an opportunity to engage with an international leadership network while addressing a critical national challenge.

The initiative places particular emphasis on entrepreneurs as drivers of employment, recognising that young business leaders can contribute directly to creating livelihoods and expanding economic opportunities for other young people.

Eligible entrepreneurs should carefully review the requirements and submit their applications before the 12 September 2026 deadline.

The One Young World Summit will take place in Cape Town from 3–6 November 2026, providing selected participants with an opportunity to engage with a global community of young leaders while contributing to conversations and solutions around entrepreneurship, employment and youth unemployment.

item.content:encoded:
The Embassy of the Czech Republic in Pretoria has officially opened applications for the Small-Scale Development Projects (SSP) 2027, offering financial support to eligible organisations implementing community-focused development initiatives across nine African countries.

Through this annual call for proposals, eligible non-governmental and non-political organisations can apply for a Czech financial contribution ranging from CZK 200,000 to CZK 500,000 to implement projects that respond to local development priorities, particularly initiatives focused on skills development, community development and job creation.

The programme forms part of the Development Cooperation of the Czech Republic and is designed to support practical, locally driven projects capable of producing sustainable benefits for communities.

Applications are open to eligible organisations in Angola, Botswana, Eswatini, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa.

The deadline for submission of complete proposals is 15 September 2026.

About the Czech Republic Small-Scale Development Projects 2027

The Small-Scale Project, commonly referred to as SSP, is one of the instruments used within the Development Cooperation framework of the Czech Republic.

The programme provides an opportunity for locally established organisations to propose relatively small but targeted development projects that can contribute meaningfully to communities.

Potential implementers submit their applications to the relevant Embassy of the Czech Republic. Proposed projects are identified by the respective Czech embassies and subsequently submitted for approval by the headquarters of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic.

For the 2027 funding round administered by the Embassy of the Czech Republic in Pretoria, the programme covers all countries accredited to the Embassy.

These are:

  • Angola
  • Botswana
  • Eswatini
  • Madagascar
  • Mauritius
  • Mozambique
  • Lesotho
  • Namibia
  • South Africa

The intention is not simply to provide short-term financial assistance. Proposed projects should contribute to local communities through development activities that correspond with the national development priorities of the country in which the project will be implemented.

How Much Funding Is Available?

Successful projects may receive a financial contribution from the Czech Republic ranging from:

CZK 200,000 to CZK 500,000 per project.

Applicants should develop realistic project budgets that demonstrate how the requested funding will be used to achieve clear development objectives.

The Embassy also states that co-financing from other sources is desirable, although the level of such co-financing is at the discretion of the applicant.

This means organisations that have access to their own resources or additional funding partners may incorporate those resources into the proposed project.

Applicants should, however, pay careful attention to the financial conditions of the programme, including restrictions on administrative expenses and personnel-related expenditure.

Priority Areas for Small-Scale Projects 2027

Projects submitted under the programme should align with the relevant development priorities of the country where implementation will take place.

Particular emphasis is being placed on projects addressing:

  • Skills development
  • Community development
  • Job creation
  • Local development priorities
  • Sustainable community impact

Applicants should therefore demonstrate a clear connection between their proposed activities and the needs of the communities they intend to support.

Projects should not be designed solely around short-term activities. Sustainability is an important requirement of the programme.

Sustainability Is a Key Requirement

One of the most important conditions of the Czech Republic Small-Scale Development Projects programme is sustainability.

According to the Embassy, a project must be capable of continuing without further financial support from the Czech Republic.

Applicants should therefore consider what will happen after the funding period ends.

A strong proposal should explain how the benefits, activities, skills, infrastructure or other outcomes created through the project will continue after Czech financial assistance has concluded.

Depending on the nature of the project, sustainability could involve strengthening the capacity of a local organisation, providing communities with skills they can continue using, establishing income-generating activities, developing systems that can operate independently or creating assets that provide benefits beyond the project period.

The precise sustainability model will depend on the proposed project, but applicants should make this an important part of their project planning.

Who Can Implement an SSP Project?

The programme is intended for organisations rather than individual applicants.

The implementer must be a non-governmental and non-political organisation with legal personality in the country where the project will be implemented.

This is particularly important because applicants are required to submit documentation proving their legal status.

The organisation must also be eligible to enter into a contract with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic (MFA CZ).

The resulting agreement establishes the jurisdiction of Czech laws and courts.

Applicants should carefully consider this requirement before submitting a proposal, as successful organisations will be entering into a formal contractual relationship.

Eligible Countries for the 2027 Call

The Embassy of the Czech Republic in Pretoria is accepting applications relating to projects in the following countries:

  1. Angola
  2. Botswana
  3. Eswatini
  4. Madagascar
  5. Mauritius
  6. Mozambique
  7. Lesotho
  8. Namibia
  9. South Africa

Applicants should ensure that their organisation has the required legal personality in the country where the proposed project will be implemented.

Project Implementation Period

The anticipated implementation period for successful projects is:

March to October 2027.

However, implementation cannot begin simply because an applicant has been selected.

Projects may commence only after the relevant contract has been signed.

Successful applicants are expected to sign a contract with the Embassy of the Czech Republic during the first quarter of 2027.

Furthermore, the project must be fully implemented and all funds properly accounted for by:

15 October 2027.

Organisations developing their implementation schedules should therefore ensure that all proposed activities, procurement, programme delivery and financial accounting can realistically be completed within the permitted timeframe.

Important Financial and Implementation Conditions

Applicants should carefully review the programme’s financial and implementation requirements before preparing a budget.

1. Administrative Costs Cannot Be Funded

Administrative costs incurred by the implementing organisation cannot be covered by the SSP funding.

Applicants should therefore structure their budgets carefully and distinguish eligible project expenditure from general organisational administrative expenses.

2. Personnel and Expert-Related Costs Are Limited

Costs associated with experts should be kept as low as possible.

This includes:

  • Salaries or professional fees
  • Allowances
  • Accommodation
  • Travel costs
  • Insurance, where applicable
  • Vaccination expenses, where applicable

Collectively, these expenses must not exceed 25% of the project’s total costs.

Applicants should carefully calculate this proportion before submitting their budget.

3. The CZK Funding Amount Is Binding

The total amount of funding provided in Czech koruna (CZK) is binding when funds are converted into another currency.

Organisations working with local currencies should therefore be mindful of exchange rates and potential currency fluctuations when preparing and subsequently implementing their budgets.

4. Projects Must Be Sustainable

The project must be designed so that it can continue delivering benefits without requiring additional financial support from the Czech Republic after the funding period.

5. Czech Aid Visibility Requirements Apply

Tangible assets obtained or developed through the project must carry the Czech Aid logo.

Where a project produces intangible assets, the financial support provided through the Czech Republic Development Cooperation must be acknowledged.

Successful organisations should therefore incorporate appropriate donor visibility and acknowledgement into project implementation.

6. Full Terms Will Be Established by Contract

The complete terms and conditions governing successful projects will be detailed in the contract between the successful implementer and the relevant Czech authorities.

Required Application Documents

Applications must be submitted in English.

To be considered, applicants need to prepare a complete proposal containing all required documents.

1. SSP Identification Form

Applicants must provide two copies of the completed SSP Identification Form 2026.

The two copies must be submitted in different formats:

  • One copy must be completed, stamped, signed and scanned as a PDF file.
  • The second copy must be saved and submitted in its original XLSX spreadsheet format.

Applicants should ensure that the information contained in both versions is consistent.

2. Proof of Legal Status

Applicants must provide a copy of an official document proving the organisation’s legal status.

This requirement demonstrates that the applicant is a legally recognised entity and satisfies the requirement to have legal personality in the country where implementation will take place.

3. Authorisation of the Project Manager

Applicants must provide a document confirming that the designated contact person or project manager has been authorised to act on behalf of the institution.

The project manager must be authorised to:

  • Represent the institution in relation to the project
  • Sign the Identification Form
  • Oversee the project
  • Implement the project

Organisations should ensure that the authorisation documentation clearly establishes these responsibilities.

4. Identification Document or Passport

A copy of the ID document or passport of the designated project manager must be included with the application.

5. Evidence of Previous Development Project Experience

Applicants must provide at least three reference letters or other documentation demonstrating previous implementation of similar development projects.

This requirement means organisations should be prepared to demonstrate relevant experience rather than simply proposing a project without evidence of previous implementation capacity.

Applicants should select references or documentation that clearly demonstrate their ability to manage development activities similar to the project they are proposing.

How to Apply for the Czech Republic Small-Scale Projects 2027

Organisations interested in applying should follow the application process carefully.

Step 1: Confirm Organisational Eligibility

Before investing significant time in developing a proposal, confirm that your organisation:

  • Is non-governmental
  • Is non-political
  • Has legal personality in the country of project implementation
  • Operates in one of the nine eligible countries
  • Can enter into the required contractual arrangement
  • Has previous experience implementing similar development projects

Step 2: Develop the Project Concept

Identify a development challenge relevant to the community where the project will be implemented.

The proposal should align with national development priorities and preferably demonstrate a strong connection with the programme’s emphasis on:

  • Skills
  • Community development
  • Employment and job creation

Step 3: Develop a Sustainable Project Model

Applicants should explain how the project will create benefits beyond the funding period.

Consider what structures, skills, resources, partnerships or activities will remain after October 2027.

Step 4: Prepare a Realistic Budget

Develop the budget within the available Czech contribution of CZK 200,000 to CZK 500,000.

Remember that administrative costs cannot be funded and expert-related salaries, fees, allowances, accommodation, travel, insurance and vaccination expenses should be minimised and collectively must not exceed 25% of total project costs.

Co-financing from other sources may also be incorporated and is considered desirable.

Step 5: Complete the SSP Identification Form

Complete the required SSP Identification Form carefully.

Prepare:

  • One stamped and signed PDF version
  • One XLSX version

Applicants should review both copies before submission to make sure the information is accurate and consistent.

Step 6: Gather Supporting Documents

Prepare:

  • Proof of the organisation’s legal status
  • Proof of authorisation for the project manager
  • Project manager’s ID or passport copy
  • At least three reference letters or documents demonstrating previous implementation of similar development projects

Step 7: Submit the Complete Application

All required documents must be submitted electronically to:

smallscaleprojectscz@gmail.com

The email subject line should follow the format:

SSP 2027: [Name of the Implementer]

Applicants should make sure their submission is complete before sending it.

Application Deadline

The deadline to submit complete proposals is:

15 September 2026

Applicants should aim to submit before the deadline where possible to allow sufficient time to check that all required documentation has been attached and submitted in the correct formats.

Incomplete proposals may not satisfy the requirements for consideration.

What Happens After Applications Are Submitted?

The Small-Scale Projects are identified by the respective Czech embassies based on applications submitted by potential implementers.

Projects are subsequently subject to approval by the headquarters of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic.

Successful applicants under the Pretoria Embassy’s 2027 call are expected to enter into a contract with the Embassy during the first quarter of 2027.

Implementation can commence only after the contract has been signed.

Successful organisations will then have the March–October 2027 implementation period to deliver their approved activities, with projects and funding required to be fully accounted for by 15 October 2027.

Why Organisations Should Consider the SSP 2027 Opportunity

The Small-Scale Development Projects programme provides eligible African organisations with an opportunity to obtain international development funding for targeted initiatives at the local level.

The programme may be particularly relevant for established organisations that already have experience delivering community development initiatives and have identified practical interventions capable of producing sustainable outcomes.

The funding can help eligible organisations develop projects centred on areas such as skills development, community advancement and employment creation while contributing to national development priorities.

The requirement for sustainability also encourages organisations to design interventions whose impact can extend beyond the immediate funding period.

Important Dates at a Glance

Applicants should keep the following dates and periods in mind:

  • Call published: 28 August 2026
  • Call updated: 1 September 2026
  • Application deadline: 15 September 2026
  • Contract signing for successful applicants: First quarter of 2027
  • Project implementation period: March–October 2027
  • Final implementation and accounting deadline: 15 October 2027

Important Advice Before Submitting

Applicants should carefully review every requirement before sending their proposal.

In particular, organisations should ensure that:

  • The application is completed in English.
  • The organisation has legal personality in the project country.
  • The organisation is non-governmental and non-political.
  • The proposed project addresses relevant national development priorities.
  • The proposal clearly demonstrates sustainability.
  • The requested Czech contribution falls between CZK 200,000 and CZK 500,000.
  • Administrative expenses are not included as funded costs.
  • Relevant expert and personnel-related expenses remain within the 25% limit.
  • The SSP Identification Form is provided in both required formats.
  • The signed version contains the necessary stamp and signature.
  • All required supporting documents are attached.
  • At least three references or supporting documents showing previous similar development project experience are provided.
  • The correct email subject format is used.
  • The complete application is submitted by 15 September 2026.

APPLY NOW

Conclusion

The Czech Republic Small-Scale Development Projects 2027 call offers established local organisations across nine African countries an opportunity to secure CZK 200,000 to CZK 500,000 for targeted community development initiatives.

Administered through the Embassy of the Czech Republic in Pretoria as part of the Czech Republic’s development cooperation activities, the programme is particularly focused on projects that respond to national and local development priorities, with emphasis on skills development, community development and job creation.

Successful proposals will need to go beyond identifying an immediate community need. Applicants must demonstrate appropriate legal status, previous development project experience, realistic financial planning and, importantly, the ability of the proposed initiative to remain sustainable without further Czech financial support.

Eligible organisations in Angola, Botswana, Eswatini, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa should begin preparing their documentation as soon as possible because the application window is relatively short.

Complete applications must be submitted by 15 September 2026.

Interested organisations should consult the official announcement from the Embassy of the Czech Republic in Pretoria and download the required SSP Identification Form before preparing their submission.

Visit the OFY website for more Grant Opportunities.
