item.content:encoded:
Unilever has opened applications for its 2027 Early Career Opportunities in Singapore, offering students and recent graduates the chance to build professional experience at one of the world’s largest consumer goods companies. The current Singapore recruitment campaign includes the Unilever Future Leaders Programme (UFLP) for graduates and the Unilever Leadership Internship Programme (ULIP) for university students.

These programmes provide two different entry routes into Unilever. The Future Leaders Programme is designed for graduates who want to develop toward future business leadership positions through structured development, rotations and challenging assignments. The Leadership Internship Programme, meanwhile, provides Bachelor’s and Master’s students with six months of practical experience across several business functions.

Applications opened in September 2026 for opportunities beginning in 2027.

Application period: Applications opened on 1 September 2026. Unilever’s campaign materials indicate applications through 30 September 2026, while the current Workday posting for the Future Leaders Programme technically displays an end date of 1 October 2026. Applicants are therefore strongly advised to submit by 30 September 2026 rather than relying on the system’s later closing timestamp.

Location: Singapore

UFLP intake: July 2027

ULIP internship period: 11 January 2027 to 30 June 2027

About Unilever Singapore Early Career Opportunities 2027

Unilever’s Early Careers recruitment is designed to bring emerging talent into areas that directly contribute to the company’s brands, customers, operations and long-term business development.

The Singapore Early Careers listings currently include a graduate leadership opportunity and six Leadership Internship Programme functions. These cover Marketing, Finance, Human Resources, Customer Development, Consumer Market Insights and Supply Chain/Procurement.

For applicants, this means the 2027 recruitment is not limited to one academic background or professional interest. Depending on the programme selected, candidates may work on brand development, consumer research, financial analytics, people management, sales and customer strategy, supply-chain transformation or procurement.

Unilever Future Leaders Programme – Marketing, Singapore

The Unilever Future Leaders Programme – Marketing is the principal graduate opportunity included in the current Singapore Early Careers recruitment.

The programme is intended to accelerate the development of individuals who demonstrate the potential to progress toward business leadership roles. Instead of remaining in a narrowly defined entry-level position, participants gain experience through challenging assignments and multiple job rotations.

The Singapore Marketing posting identifies the programme as a three-year programme, while Unilever’s description of the broader UFLP model refers to a typical duration of approximately two to three years.

The programme intake is scheduled for July 2027.

What Is the Unilever Future Leaders Programme?

The Unilever Future Leaders Programme focuses on developing tomorrow’s leaders by exposing participants to real business responsibilities at an early stage in their careers.

Successful applicants can expect a combination of:

  • Structured professional development
  • Job rotations across relevant business areas
  • Hands-on exposure to real commercial challenges
  • Learning from experienced Unilever colleagues and leaders
  • Formal learning programmes designed to develop leadership and business skills
  • Exposure to sales and go-to-market activities
  • Opportunities for broader or international exposure depending on programme requirements
  • Responsibility for projects with measurable business relevance

Unilever states that the programme is intended to accelerate participants’ readiness for future leadership responsibilities.

UFLP Marketing: What Participants Will Work On

Marketing at Unilever goes beyond conventional advertising. The function combines consumer understanding, data, brand strategy, communication and commercial execution.

UFLP Marketing participants may gain experience in areas such as brand building and brand development, including helping create strategic visions for brands and developing plans across the full marketing mix.

Participants may also manage projects involving external creative agencies and contribute to the coordination of product launches with supply-chain and category teams.

The work is therefore suited to graduates who are interested in understanding consumers, interpreting market information and translating insights into strategies that strengthen brand equity and generate business demand.

UFLP Marketing Eligibility Requirements

For the Singapore Future Leaders Programme – Marketing, Unilever currently identifies several core requirements.

Applicants must have at least a Bachelor’s degree.

The programme is intended for graduates with no more than 24 months of formal work experience after graduation.

Candidates should also demonstrate energy, motivation and leadership potential and be willing to travel where required. Geographic mobility is specifically identified as an expectation for applicants.

This makes UFLP particularly relevant to new graduates and early-career professionals rather than applicants who already have several years of full-time post-graduation professional experience.

UFLP Marketing Selection Process

Applicants should expect a multi-stage recruitment process.

Unilever currently identifies the process as:

  1. Online application
  2. Blended assessments
  3. Digital interview
  4. Phone interview
  5. Discovery Centre

The Discovery Centre is expected to be conducted physically in October 2026.

Applicants should therefore plan for more than simply submitting a CV. Candidates may be assessed on problem-solving, communication, decision-making, motivation and leadership potential throughout the process.

Unilever also warns candidates that submitting duplicate applications for the same position or applying to multiple UFLP functions may affect the review process or eligibility.

Unilever Leadership Internship Programme 2027

Students who are still completing their university education can apply for the Unilever Leadership Internship Programme, commonly known as ULIP.

Unlike UFLP, which is designed for graduates entering a longer leadership-development programme, ULIP is a six-month internship programme.

The internship is scheduled to run from:

11 January 2027 to 30 June 2027.

The current Singapore recruitment includes six major areas:

  1. Marketing
  2. Finance
  3. Human Resources
  4. Customer Development
  5. Consumer Market Insights
  6. Supply Chain/Procurement

These opportunities appear within Unilever’s Singapore Early Careers recruitment portal.

1. Unilever Leadership Internship Programme – Marketing

The Marketing internship is designed for students interested in consumer behaviour, brands, digital marketing, communication and commercial strategy.

Interns can gain exposure to how Unilever’s brand teams understand consumers, interpret data and design campaigns intended to build demand and brand equity.

Work may involve:

  • Brand building and brand development
  • Developing plans across the marketing mix
  • Consumer and market analysis
  • Supporting advertising and communications
  • Working with external creative agencies
  • Supporting product launches
  • Digitalisation and marketing technology projects

Examples cited by Unilever from previous ULIP Marketing projects include applying AI and augmented reality technologies to beauty-related consumer experiences, supporting engagement plans for a CLEAR product in Indonesia, and developing digital brand-health dashboards for Southeast Asian brands.

The examples demonstrate that interns may be given commercially relevant assignments rather than purely administrative duties.

2. Unilever Leadership Internship Programme – Finance

The Finance internship gives students experience in how a major multinational organisation protects and creates value while managing sustainable financial performance.

Students may work with experienced finance professionals and other business teams to analyse information and support decision-making.

Examples of previous ULIP Finance projects cited by Unilever include:

  • Automating inventory analytics to support inventory management and business-waste governance
  • Partnering with business groups to provide financial insights and analysis
  • Creating Power BI dashboards for price analytics, benchmarking and governance

The six-month Finance internship is based in Singapore.

This opportunity may be particularly relevant for students interested in corporate finance, management accounting, business analytics, financial planning, performance management and data-driven decision-making.

3. Unilever Leadership Internship Programme – Human Resources

The Human Resources internship allows students to work on projects related to Unilever’s people, organisational culture, talent and employee experience.

Interns may contribute to strategic HR initiatives while working alongside experienced leaders and business teams.

Unilever identifies examples of previous intern assignments including supporting talent-development forums and change-management initiatives, improving employee experiences through policy implementation and onboarding, contributing to recruitment activities, supporting long-service recognition programmes and participating in employer-branding initiatives both on and off university campuses.

The role offers exposure to the connection between HR strategy and organisational performance rather than treating HR simply as an administrative function.

4. Unilever Leadership Internship Programme – Customer Development

Customer Development is closely connected with how Unilever brings its brands and products to customers and markets.

The Singapore internship can provide experience working in what the company describes as a “white space” business environment, involving different geographies, consumers and customers.

Students can learn how products are developed commercially, how market opportunities are identified and how partnerships contribute to business expansion.

Unilever provides examples of previous Customer Development intern projects involving commercial opportunities linked to consumers living outside their home markets and expanding route-to-market or brand-partner portfolios in major markets.

This programme may appeal particularly to students interested in sales, business development, commercial strategy, customer management and entrepreneurship.

5. Unilever Leadership Internship Programme – Consumer Market Insights

Consumer Market Insights, or CMI, focuses on transforming data and research into knowledge that can improve marketing and business decisions.

Interns may work with both primary and secondary research, analyse market dynamics and help convert findings into recommendations for Unilever’s brand teams.

The programme can involve areas such as:

  • Consumer research
  • Market analysis
  • Research design
  • Data interpretation
  • Insight generation
  • Visualisation and storytelling
  • Identifying digital and social trends
  • Working with external research agencies

Unilever’s examples include working with research organisations on questionnaires and research findings, tracking digital and social trends, creating visualisations and summaries, and assisting with systems used in research execution.

This may be particularly attractive to students interested in market research, analytics, consumer psychology and data-driven marketing strategy.

6. Unilever Leadership Internship Programme – Supply Chain/Procurement

The Supply Chain/Procurement internship provides exposure to the increasingly technology-driven environment behind the production, sourcing and movement of consumer products.

Unilever specifically highlights areas including real-time data, analytics and robotic process automation.

Previous ULIP projects have included supply-chain analysis for new business opportunities, logistics digitalisation, conversion of large datasets into more usable information, sustainable and traceable sourcing initiatives and negotiations with important suppliers.

Interns can also gain exposure to contracting and sourcing strategies.

This route may be especially relevant to students interested in procurement, logistics, operations, data analytics, sustainability and supply-chain management.

Who Can Apply for the Unilever Leadership Internship Programme?

ULIP has an important eligibility distinction from UFLP.

Applicants must currently be enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree programme.

Unilever explicitly states that fresh graduates are not eligible for ULIP internships. Therefore, students who have already completed their degree and are no longer enrolled should instead examine graduate opportunities such as UFLP where they meet the requirements.

Interns must also be able to commit to at least three days per week, although Unilever indicates that full-time participation is preferred.

Across the Singapore ULIP listings, the company also looks for applicants who can work in a fast-paced and results-oriented environment, demonstrate initiative, take on new challenges and communicate effectively in both written and verbal settings.

Part-Time and Full-Time Participation

The ULIP listings describe a six-month experience with flexibility between part-time and full-time engagement, while simultaneously requiring a commitment of at least three days per week and stating that full-time commitment is preferred.

Applicants should therefore ensure their university schedule allows them to meet the minimum attendance requirement throughout the internship period from January to June 2027.

ULIP Selection Process

The six Singapore internship functions follow a broadly consistent selection process:

  1. Online application
  2. SOVA blended assessment
  3. Phone interview
  4. Virtual interview with the hiring manager
  5. Final offer stage

Unilever indicates that successful offers are expected to be extended by approximately the first week of December 2026.

Because the internship begins on 11 January 2027, successful candidates have approximately one month between the anticipated offer stage and programme commencement.

Why Consider Unilever Early Careers?

One of the distinguishing characteristics of both UFLP and ULIP is the emphasis on actual business exposure.

ULIP descriptions repeatedly state that interns work with experienced teams and leaders on tangible projects. Examples across functions demonstrate exposure to business analytics, brand strategy, AI, consumer research, procurement, sustainability, employee experience and commercial development.

UFLP goes further by placing graduates into a structured development pathway with rotations and leadership-oriented assignments. Its purpose is not merely to provide an entry-level marketing position but to accelerate participants’ readiness for larger business responsibilities.

For students and early-career graduates seeking experience in a large multinational consumer-goods organisation, the programmes therefore provide two clearly differentiated entry routes.

Important Difference Between UFLP and ULIP

Candidates should select the programme that matches their current academic status.

UFLP is aimed at graduates. Applicants need at least a Bachelor’s degree and generally should not have more than 24 months of formal work experience after graduation. The Singapore Marketing intake begins in July 2027.

ULIP, by contrast, is specifically for students who remain enrolled in Bachelor’s or Master’s programmes. Fresh graduates are explicitly excluded from the internship route. ULIP begins on 11 January 2027 and finishes on 30 June 2027.

Candidates should therefore verify their student or graduate status carefully before submitting an application.

Application Deadline

Applications opened on 1 September 2026.

The recruitment campaign indicates an application period through 30 September 2026. The Workday system for the UFLP Marketing position currently displays an End Date of 1 October 2026. To avoid any timezone or system-closing issue, candidates should regard 30 September 2026 as the practical deadline and submit earlier whenever possible.

Applicants should also remember that recruitment processes can close or change, so the official application portal should always be checked immediately before submission.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted through Unilever’s official Early Careers recruitment portal.

Candidates should review the individual position that matches their academic status and career interests, prepare the requested application information and submit through the online system.

Official reference and application page:
Unilever Singapore Early Careers 2027 Application Portal

Candidates should apply only through official Unilever channels. Unilever also warns applicants that it does not request money or credit-card information as part of its recruitment process.

Conclusion

The Unilever Singapore Early Careers 2027 recruitment provides a significant opportunity for both university students and recent graduates seeking exposure to a major multinational consumer-goods organisation.

Graduates can pursue the Unilever Future Leaders Programme – Marketing, a multi-year development pathway beginning in July 2027 that combines leadership development, business assignments and rotations.

Students currently completing Bachelor’s or Master’s degrees can apply for the six-month Unilever Leadership Internship Programme, with opportunities available across Marketing, Finance, Human Resources, Customer Development, Consumer Market Insights and Supply Chain/Procurement.

The internship runs from 11 January to 30 June 2027, while the UFLP Marketing intake begins in July 2027. Candidates are advised to submit applications by 30 September 2026.

Applicants should carefully select the correct programme because the eligibility conditions are substantially different: UFLP is intended for graduates, while ULIP requires applicants to remain enrolled as university students.

item.content:encoded:
NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) offers students interested in building experience in science, technology, engineering and mathematics a range of internship, research and educational opportunities.

JPL’s Academic Engagement Office manages numerous internship opportunities across STEM fields, giving eligible students the opportunity to identify programmes suited to their academic level, interests and availability. The opportunities listed by JPL include year-round internships, summer internships, visiting student research programmes, partner programmes and specialised workshops.

The opportunities span undergraduate and graduate levels, while some specialised programmes are also available to doctoral students, postdoctoral participants and educators.

For students aspiring to gain exposure to research, technology and STEM careers, the JPL programmes provide several pathways worth exploring.

About NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory

The Jet Propulsion Laboratory is closely associated with NASA’s scientific and technological work and provides educational opportunities designed to connect students with STEM fields.

Through JPL Education and its Academic Engagement Office, students can explore internship programmes and other learning opportunities related to science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

Rather than offering only one internship pathway, JPL presents several programmes designed for different academic levels and periods of the year.

This means prospective applicants should carefully review the individual programme that best matches their academic status, interests and availability before applying.

What Are the JPL Internship Programs?

JPL’s internship opportunities encompass multiple programmes rather than a single internship.

The Academic Engagement Office specifically manages internship opportunities in:

  • Science
  • Technology
  • Engineering
  • Mathematics

The programmes listed by JPL include opportunities for undergraduate and graduate students, while additional partner programmes and workshops broaden the options available to other groups.

Applicants should note that requirements, schedules and application procedures may differ considerably between programmes. Students should therefore review the individual programme information rather than assuming that the eligibility criteria for one JPL opportunity apply to every programme.

JPL Year-Round Internship Program

One of the opportunities listed is the JPL Year-Round Internship Program.

The programme is identified as being available to:

  • Undergraduate students
  • Graduate students

Unlike an internship restricted to a particular season, JPL lists the session for this programme as “Any,” indicating that the opportunity is structured as a year-round programme rather than solely as a summer placement.

This can make the programme particularly relevant to students who want to investigate opportunities outside the conventional summer internship period.

Prospective applicants should consult the individual Year-Round Internship Program page for the current eligibility requirements, openings, application instructions and relevant deadlines.

JPL Summer Internship Program

Students specifically seeking a summer experience can explore the JPL Summer Internship Program.

JPL lists this programme for:

  • Undergraduate students
  • Graduate students

The designated session is Summer.

A summer programme may be especially attractive to students who want to incorporate an internship into their academic journey during the period between academic terms.

Applicants should review the programme’s dedicated page to determine current requirements and application dates before submitting an application.

JPL Visiting Student Research Program

JPL also lists the JPL Visiting Student Research Program, providing another pathway for students interested in research-oriented opportunities.

According to the programme directory, the Visiting Student Research Program is available at the:

  • Undergraduate level
  • Graduate level

The session is listed as “Any,” rather than being restricted to summer.

Students interested in research should examine the programme-specific requirements to determine whether their academic background and circumstances meet the eligibility criteria.

JPL Partner Programs

JPL’s opportunities extend beyond programmes directly presented under the primary JPL internship section.

The Academic Engagement Office also works with outside universities and organisations to make additional internship positions at the laboratory possible.

These partner opportunities broaden the range of routes through which eligible students and other participants may engage with JPL.

Among the partner programmes listed are the Caltech Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship and the NASA/IPAC Teacher Archive Research Program.

Caltech Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship

The Caltech Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship is listed by JPL as a partner programme.

It is intended for:

  • Undergraduate students

The programme session is:

  • Summer

This provides undergraduate students with another research-focused pathway associated with opportunities at the laboratory.

Because this is a partner programme, prospective applicants should pay particular attention to the specific application procedures and requirements established for the fellowship.

NASA/IPAC Teacher Archive Research Program

The opportunities listed by JPL are not limited entirely to university students.

The NASA/IPAC Teacher Archive Research Program is listed for:

  • Formal educators
  • Informal educators

JPL directs prospective participants to the individual programme details for information about its session and other requirements.

This demonstrates that JPL’s broader educational ecosystem includes opportunities that can also support educators interested in STEM learning and research.

STEM Workshops Available Through JPL

In addition to internships and partner programmes, JPL highlights workshops designed to help students gain a deeper educational understanding of STEM careers.

According to JPL, these workshops are intended to provide students with an in-depth look at careers in science, technology, engineering and mathematics and help them define potential career paths.

Two programmes highlighted in this category are:

  1. NASA Community College Aerospace Scholars
  2. NASA Science Mission Design Schools

These programmes target different academic audiences.

NASA Community College Aerospace Scholars

The NASA Community College Aerospace Scholars programme is listed at the undergraduate academic level.

Students interested in this programme should consult its dedicated programme information for details regarding sessions, eligibility and participation requirements.

This programme represents another route through which undergraduate students can investigate educational experiences connected with NASA and aerospace-related STEM pathways.

NASA Science Mission Design Schools

JPL also lists NASA Science Mission Design Schools among its workshop opportunities.

This opportunity targets more advanced academic levels, including:

  • Graduate students
  • Doctoral students
  • Postdoctoral participants

The JPL directory directs prospective applicants to the programme-specific details for session information.

This makes the programme particularly relevant to individuals who have progressed beyond the undergraduate stage and are seeking advanced educational experiences related to science missions.

NASA Internship Programs

In addition to the JPL-specific opportunities, the page directs students to the broader NASA Internship Programs.

NASA Internship Programs are listed for:

  • Undergraduate students
  • Graduate students

Sessions are available during:

  • Fall
  • Spring
  • Summer

This gives students multiple periods during the academic year in which they may be able to explore NASA internship opportunities.

Students should distinguish between the individual JPL programmes and the broader NASA internship opportunities and review the relevant programme page before applying.

Academic Levels Covered by the Opportunities

Taken together, the programmes listed by JPL cover several academic and professional stages.

Depending on the specific opportunity, participants may include:

  • Undergraduate students
  • Graduate students
  • Doctoral students
  • Postdoctoral participants
  • Formal educators
  • Informal educators

However, these categories should not be interpreted as universal eligibility across all programmes.

For example, the JPL Summer Internship Program is listed for undergraduate and graduate students, while NASA Science Mission Design Schools extend to graduate, doctoral and postdoctoral levels.

Applicants must therefore select the appropriate programme first and then confirm its individual eligibility requirements.

When Are the JPL Internship Programs Offered?

Availability depends on the programme.

The JPL programme directory identifies several scheduling formats, including:

  • Year-round/Any session: Some programmes, including the JPL Year-Round Internship Program and JPL Visiting Student Research Program, are listed under “Any.”
  • Summer: The JPL Summer Internship Program and Caltech Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship are listed for summer.
  • Fall, Spring and Summer: The broader NASA Internship Programs are listed across all three sessions.
  • Programme-specific schedules: Certain workshops and partner programmes require applicants to consult their dedicated programme details.

Because programme schedules can differ, students should avoid relying on a single application timeline for all JPL opportunities.

How to Choose the Right JPL Program

With multiple programmes available, prospective applicants should begin by determining which opportunity corresponds most closely with their academic stage and objectives.

A useful approach is to:

  1. Identify your academic level. Determine whether you fall into the undergraduate, graduate, doctoral, postdoctoral or educator category.
  2. Determine what type of experience you want. Consider whether you are looking for an internship, research experience, partner programme or educational workshop.
  3. Consider your availability. Decide whether you need a summer programme, a year-round opportunity or another session.
  4. Review the individual programme page. Programme-specific eligibility, application requirements and timelines may differ.
  5. Prepare your application materials carefully. Follow the instructions for your selected programme rather than using assumptions based on another JPL opportunity.

Resources for Prospective JPL Interns

JPL provides additional resources to help students understand internship opportunities and prepare their applications.

JPL Internships FAQ

Students who have questions about the internship process can consult JPL’s Internships FAQ, which provides answers to commonly asked questions about JPL internship programmes.

Reviewing the FAQ before applying may help candidates better understand programme expectations and resolve common questions.

How to Get a JPL Internship

JPL also provides a guide titled How to Get a JPL Internship.

The resource is designed to introduce prospective applicants to the world of JPL internships and provide guidance on positioning themselves for internship opportunities.

Students considering an application should review this resource as part of their preparation.

Resume Guidelines

A strong resume can be an important component of internship preparation.

JPL’s Academic Engagement Office provides Resume Guidelines containing tips and best practices for writing an effective resume.

Applicants can use these guidelines when preparing or reviewing their resume before applying to an appropriate opportunity.

Additional Opportunities for Students and Researchers

Students who do not find a suitable opportunity among the main programmes can also explore additional resources highlighted by JPL.

These include:

  • Opportunities for students through JPL Careers
  • Caltech Student-Faculty Programs
  • JPL Postdoctoral Programs
  • JPL Careers
  • Careers at NASA

JPL specifically provides links to its careers platform, Caltech’s Student-Faculty Programs and JPL’s postdoctoral programmes as additional routes for individuals seeking relevant opportunities.

How to Apply for JPL Internship Opportunities

There is not one universal application process described on the supplied JPL programme directory for every opportunity listed.

Instead, prospective candidates should:

  1. Visit JPL’s Explore Programs & Apply directory.
  2. Review the available JPL programmes, partner programmes, workshops and NASA programmes.
  3. Select the opportunity matching their academic level.
  4. Open the individual programme page.
  5. Carefully review its current eligibility requirements and programme details.
  6. Check the applicable session and application timeline.
  7. Prepare any materials required by that specific programme.
  8. Follow the programme’s official application instructions.

Applicants should rely on the requirements displayed for the specific programme they intend to pursue.

APPLY NOW

Application Deadline

There is no single application deadline stated on the supplied JPL Explore Programs & Apply page.

This is important because the page covers numerous programmes with different sessions and programme structures.

Some opportunities are listed as year-round, some operate during summer, while broader NASA internships are available in fall, spring and summer. Applicants should therefore visit the individual programme page to identify the applicable application deadline and confirm that applications are currently being accepted.

Why Students Should Explore the JPL Programs

For students pursuing STEM education, the breadth of opportunities presented through JPL makes the programme directory worth exploring.

Rather than limiting students to one pathway, the directory brings together:

  • Year-round internship opportunities
  • Summer internships
  • Visiting student research opportunities
  • Partner research programmes
  • Opportunities for educators
  • Undergraduate STEM workshops
  • Advanced programmes for graduate, doctoral and postdoctoral participants
  • Broader NASA internship programmes
  • Internship preparation resources
  • Additional JPL and Caltech opportunities

The variety allows prospective participants to search for an opportunity based on their current academic level, career goals and availability.

Conclusion

NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory offers a broad collection of internship, research and educational pathways for people interested in science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

Through the JPL Academic Engagement Office, undergraduate and graduate students can explore the JPL Year-Round Internship Program, JPL Summer Internship Program and JPL Visiting Student Research Program. Partner opportunities add further pathways, while specialised workshops extend the programme landscape to additional academic groups and educators.

Students can also explore NASA Internship Programs, which are listed for undergraduate and graduate students during fall, spring and summer sessions.

Because these opportunities have different academic levels, schedules and programme structures, applicants should carefully review the individual programme that interests them before applying. The supplied programme directory does not state one universal deadline, so candidates should check the official programme-specific pages for current application periods, requirements and deadlines.

For students seeking to build their experience in STEM and explore opportunities connected with NASA and JPL, the Explore Programs & Apply directory provides a valuable starting point for identifying the programme that best matches their academic and professional journey.

Visit the OFY website for more Internship Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The Migration Policy Institute (MPI) is inviting applications for its prestigious Demetrios G. Papademetriou Young Scholars Program 2027, offering aspiring researchers, policy professionals, communicators, and migration specialists an opportunity to gain practical experience in one of the world’s leading independent think tanks focused on migration and human mobility.

The program provides paid internship opportunities for individuals interested in migration policy, refugee and asylum issues, immigrant integration, international development, public policy, communications, and related fields. Interns have the opportunity to contribute directly to meaningful research, policy analysis, communications initiatives, events, and public engagement activities while working alongside experienced professionals.

One of the notable features of the MPI internship program is its international accessibility. Internships are available both remotely and in person, and individuals residing outside the United States may also be eligible to participate under the program’s applicable work and residency requirements.

For the Spring 2027 internship cycle, interested applicants must submit their applications by October 15, 2026.

About the Migration Policy Institute

The Migration Policy Institute is an independent, nonpartisan, and nonprofit think tank dedicated to improving migration and mobility policies around the world. MPI conducts research and analysis on major migration-related issues and provides policymakers, practitioners, researchers, and the public with evidence-based insights into immigration systems and global mobility.

The Institute works across a broad range of issues, including:

  • Immigration policy and systems
  • Refugee protection and asylum
  • Border management and migration enforcement
  • Immigrant integration
  • Education and workforce development
  • International migration
  • Labor migration
  • Migration and development
  • Refugee and forced displacement
  • Social cohesion
  • Language access
  • Returns and reintegration

Through its research, publications, events, and policy engagement, MPI contributes to discussions and decision-making on some of the most important migration challenges facing societies worldwide.

About the Demetrios G. Papademetriou Young Scholars Program

The internship program is named in honor of Demetrios G. Papademetriou, the founding president of the Migration Policy Institute.

The Young Scholars Program was established to pursue two important objectives:

  1. To benefit from the perspectives, skills, and contributions of talented interns supporting MPI’s work.
  2. To help train and prepare the next generation of migration researchers, policy experts, and communications professionals.

The program reflects MPI’s commitment to mentorship and professional development by providing emerging professionals with meaningful exposure to migration research, policy discussions, communications, and public engagement.

The internship program was officially named the Demetrios G. Papademetriou Young Scholars Program in 2021. Papademetriou led MPI from its establishment in 2001 until 2014 and continued serving as President Emeritus and Distinguished Transatlantic Fellow until his death.

Throughout his career, he demonstrated a strong commitment to mentoring and supporting emerging migration thinkers and policy professionals. The Young Scholars Program continues this legacy by creating opportunities for young and early-career professionals to develop their expertise and build careers in migration-related fields.

MPI Internship Program Areas

Research interns can work across several specialized program areas at the Migration Policy Institute. These areas provide opportunities to explore different dimensions of migration policy and develop expertise in specific fields.

1. U.S. Immigration

Interns working in the U.S. Immigration program may contribute to research and policy analysis relating to major immigration issues in the United States.

Areas of focus may include:

  • Asylum systems
  • Refugee pathways
  • Border management
  • Immigration enforcement
  • Legal immigration
  • Temporary and permanent migration pathways
  • Unauthorized immigration
  • Employment outcomes of highly educated immigrants
  • Immigration and demographic trends
  • Economic trends related to migration
  • Policy reform proposals

This program is particularly relevant for applicants interested in immigration law, public policy, political science, economics, sociology, and migration studies.

2. International Migration

The International Migration program focuses on comparative migration policies and global mobility challenges.

Research may address areas such as:

  • Refugee resettlement
  • Asylum systems
  • Immigrant integration
  • Labor market integration
  • Social cohesion
  • Labor migration
  • Borders and mobility
  • Migration and development
  • Returns and reintegration

Interns may gain exposure to comparative policy analysis and international migration systems while examining how governments and institutions respond to migration challenges across different regions.

3. U.S. Immigrant Integration

The U.S. Immigrant Integration program focuses on policies and systems that influence how immigrants integrate into communities, education systems, and labor markets.

Research areas may include:

  • Early childhood education and care
  • Dual Language Learners
  • English Learners
  • K-12 immigrant education
  • Adult education
  • Workforce development
  • Professional training
  • State and local immigration policies
  • Integration services
  • Language access policies

This program may be particularly suitable for individuals interested in education policy, social policy, workforce development, immigrant integration, and community development.

4. Latin America and Caribbean Initiative

The Latin America and Caribbean Initiative examines migration dynamics and policy responses across Latin America and the Caribbean.

Key areas of work include:

  • Mixed migration flows
  • Migration from northern Central America
  • Venezuelan migration
  • Migration management systems
  • Host-country responses
  • Regional development policies
  • Immigrant integration
  • Challenges and opportunities affecting migrants and host communities

The initiative pays particular attention to countries such as:

  • Mexico
  • Costa Rica
  • Colombia
  • Venezuela
  • Countries in northern Central America

Applicants interested in this program should note that written proficiency and oral fluency in Spanish are required.

5. Refugee and Forced Displacement Initiative

The Refugee and Forced Displacement Initiative focuses on research and policy approaches affecting refugees and forcibly displaced populations.

The initiative examines issues including:

  • Refugee agency
  • Lived experiences of displaced populations
  • Refugee livelihoods
  • Economic self-reliance
  • Host-country integration
  • Global refugee responses
  • The role of faith in responding to forced displacement

This program offers an opportunity for emerging researchers and policy professionals to engage with some of the world’s most pressing humanitarian and displacement challenges.

What Do MPI Research Interns Do?

Research interns play an active role in supporting the Institute’s research and policy work. Rather than simply observing organizational activities, interns may contribute to projects and research initiatives across their assigned program areas.

Typical responsibilities include:

  • Conducting independent quantitative research
  • Conducting qualitative research
  • Supporting policy analysis
  • Contributing to broader MPI research projects
  • Preparing literature reviews and summaries
  • Drafting research papers and other written materials
